items.title: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week
items.description: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”. The building, which was also attacked last Thursday , is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Houthis restarted in July. Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported Tuesday’s injuries and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF). The image showed some damage to the building about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact from a strike on the same tower on Nov 19, which caused damage but no injuries. Reuters could not immediately determine when the image was taken or the extent of the further damage from the latest strike. Saudi Civil Defence said the 11 people injured included two Saudi citizens, four Egyptian nationals, three Nepalese nationals and two Indian nationals. “Relevant authorities responded to the incident immediately, implementing all established protocols and measures for handling such situations, and taking the necessary steps to ensure the safety of lives and property,” the Arabic statement said. “One of the towers in the financial centre was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack,” coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a social media post, without naming the building. Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower is the most prominent landmark of King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD), a showcase for Saudi Arabia’s economic ambitions. A witness told AFP that a vehicle fitted with a speaker had warned pedestrians in the area to take cover on Tuesday. No warning was sent to mobile phones about any threats to the capital. Afterwards, police cars blocked some entrances to the gleaming financial district. With imposing skyscrapers, luxury shops and green spaces, the district also hosts the headquarters of the Saudi stock exchange along with multinationals such as Goldman Sachs. An attack on the PIF is symbolic as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy — a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes. A tower belonging to state oil giant Aramco in KAFD was hit earlier this month, while Riyadh’s international airport was repeatedly struck in October, with one attack killing 14 people . The Houthis, who control much of western Yemen including the capital Sanaa, have been firing at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen’s frozen civil war reignited in July in a knock-on from the US-Iran war. The attacks have caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh, and forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including soccer’s AFC Asian Cup. Such cowardly attacks undermine peace efforts: Pakistan Pakistan strongly condemned the “terrorist attack carried out today by the Houthi militia”, the Foreign Office said. In a statement, FO said Islamabad denounced “such cowardly attacks, which endanger civilians and civilian infrastructure, heighten regional tensions and undermine efforts to restore peace and stability”. “Pakistan stands in full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in the face of these attacks. The Kingdom has every right to defend its territory and protect its citizens and residents,” FO affirmed. It expressed Pakistan’s deep sympathies with those injured and their families and wished them swift and full recovery. FO also commended the Saudi authorities for their “prompt response” and the steps taken to protect lives and property. Islamabad has condemned Houthi attacks repeatedly , including on international platforms , and termed them a grave violation of the kingdom’s sovereignty. Pakistan and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye. Under the Makkah Defence Alliance, Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish leaders met in Riyadh in October and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom. Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said later that month. ‘26 killed in Yemen attack’ On the ground in Yemen, the war has caused a major humanitarian crisis, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced from their homes since July. The Houthis have seized swathes of territory, forcing forces aligned with the internationally recognised government to stage a major retreat this month. The Saudi-led military coalition has been striking Houthi targets in the impoverished country. On Tuesday, local officials said a coalition airstrike on buses and trucks killed 26 people in Lahj province. On the other hand, government forces blamed the Houthis for the attack. As the conflict shows no sign of slowing, Britain sanctioned the Houthis and four of its top officials “for deliberately attempting to undermine stability” on Tuesday. The measures include an asset freeze against the group and an asset freeze and travel ban on four figures, including security and intelligence head Abdul Hakim Hashem Ali al-Khaiwani, and interior affairs official Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi. The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015, after the Houthis had captured the capital Sanaa and sent the internationally recognised government fleeing to Aden. The war left hundreds of thousands dead and triggered a humanitarian catastrophe before an uneasy ceasefire went into effect in 2022.

items.title: Ghana Maritime Authority moves to operationalise 12-nautical-mile fishing exclusion zone to protect artisanal fishers
items.description: The Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) has begun steps to update the country’s official maritime charts to reflect the boundaries of the 12-nautical-mile Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ), as part of efforts to strengthen enforcement and protect artisanal fishing activities along the coast. The move was announced following a multi-stakeholder dialogue organised by the GMA with support from Oceana Ghana to address outstanding technical and administrative requirements for the full implementation of the protected zone. The Authority said it had initiated the chart update process following a request from the Fisheries Commission, to ensure that the designated boundaries are formally recognised by all users of Ghana’s maritime space. The engagement brought together government regulators, security agencies, industrial trawler operators, artisanal fishers and civil society organisations to assess progress, clarify institutional responsibilities and identify the remaining steps towards effective protection of coastal fishing waters. The GMA also stressed the need for stronger coordination among regulatory and enforcement agencies responsible for monitoring activities within Ghana’s waters. The dialogue formed part of Oceana Ghana’s Make The EEZ Real campaign, which supports state institutions in translating legal protections into practical safeguards for fishing communities. Although the responsibility for operationalising and enforcing the zone rests primarily with government authorities, Oceana’s support is intended to complement institutional efforts through transparency, public awareness and coordinated action. Representatives of the GMA, the Ministry for Fisheries and Aquaculture, the Fisheries Commission, the Environmental Protection Agency, the Minerals Commission, the Petroleum Commission and relevant maritime security and enforcement agencies participated in the engagement. Other participants included the National Fisheries Association of Ghana (NAFAG), the Ghana Industrial Trawlers Association, canoe owners, artisanal fishers, fish processors, civil society organisations and development partners. The 12-nautical-mile exclusion zone was established under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146), enacted in August 2025 to provide a stronger legislative framework for the sustainable management of Ghana’s marine resources. On December 29, 2025, the Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture issued Gazette Notification No. 414, officially designating all waters within the 12-nautical-mile limit, approximately 22 kilometres, as the Inshore Exclusion Zone. The zone is reserved exclusively for small-scale artisanal fishers and canoe operators, with industrial trawler vessels prohibited from fishing within the designated waters. The restriction is intended to keep large commercial fishing vessels away from near-shore breeding and nursery grounds, protect fragile marine habitats and allow depleted fish stocks to replenish. It is also expected to reduce fatal collisions between industrial trawlers and wooden fishing canoes, as well as damage to fishing equipment. However, the GMA says the legal designation alone is insufficient to guarantee protection, noting that further technical and administrative processes, alongside effective collaboration among relevant stakeholders, must be completed to translate the policy into tangible protection at sea.

items.title: PSC appoints CP Usman Adamu Zamfara Police Commissioner
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State. The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections. According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety. Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police. The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani. items.title: Lutte contre la désinformation : vers la création d’un réseau africain de jeunes journalistes
items.description: Mettre en place un Réseau africain des jeunes journalistes, ouvert aux jeunes professionnels des médias du continent, afin de renforcer la coopération, le partage d’expériences et les initiatives communes mais aussi, de lutter contre la désinformation et les discours de haine ; c’est l’ambition dévoilée à Dakar à l’issue de la première édition de la Conférence africaine des jeunes journalistes (CAJJ). Les jeunes reporters de l’Afrique se sont réunis à Dakar du 23 au 24 novembre 2026, afin d’examiner les défis majeurs liés à la propagation des discours de haine, à l’intégrité de l’information et au droit du public à une information plurielle et fiable. « Dans cette même dynamique, afin de poursuivre le plaidoyer, nous avons décidé de mettre en place un Réseau africain des jeunes journalistes, ouvert aux jeunes professionnels des médias du continent, afin de renforcer la coopération, le partage d’expériences et les initiatives communes », ont-ils annoncé dans une déclaration conjointe rendue publique mardi. Au-delà, ces jeunes journalistes souhaitent développer des mécanismes de veille, de vérification des faits et de lutte contre les campagnes de désinformation et les discours de haine. Ils veulent promouvoir des formations, des rencontres et des échanges réguliers pour renforcer les capacités de leurs membres. A lire aussi : Bakary Sarr : « Les pouvoirs publics doivent contribuer à créer les conditions d’un exercice libre et responsable du journalisme » « Porter une voix collective dans les débats africains et internationaux sur l’avenir du journalisme, la liberté de la presse et l’intégrité de l’information ; faire de la solidarité, de la responsabilité et de l’engagement professionnel les piliers de notre action commune » ; restent également des objectifs qu’ils se sont fixés à l’issue de la rencontre de Dakar. Sur ce, ils appellent tous les jeunes journalistes africains, les organisations professionnelles, les écoles de journalisme, les médias et les partenaires engagés pour la liberté de la presse à les rejoindre et à soutenir cette dynamique. « Nous sommes convaincus que l’avenir du journalisme africain ne peut se construire sans une jeunesse informée, formée, solidaire et résolument engagée pour la défense de la démocratie et de l’État de droit. De Dakar, nous lançons donc ce message d’unité et d’espérance. Face à la désinformation, opposons la vérité ; face à la haine, opposons le dialogue ; face aux manipulations, opposons l’éthique et la responsabilité », lit-on dans la déclaration. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State. The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State. It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections. The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.” It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’ The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement. It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern. The MDPCO accused the APC leadership of failing to take decisive action against members allegedly involved in political violence, warning that its silence could further embolden those responsible. “This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition,” it said. The organisation warned that Nigerians would not accept the use of violence or insecurity as instruments of electoral conquest, insisting that political parties must respect citizens’ freedom to choose their leaders. It declared that the resort to violence would not alter what it described as Nigerians’ determination to vote the APC out of power. “The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said. It demanded an immediate end to what it described as attempts to suppress democratic participation, while urging Nigerians to support its principal, Engr. Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), whom it said would reset the country through a government committed to transparency, security and citizens’ welfare. items.title: Kogi APC chieftain Kasco dumps party, joins PDP
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kogi Central has recorded a defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) following the resignation of a prominent APC chieftain, Hon. Umar Kareem, popularly known as Kasco. Kareem, from Odenk Upogoro Ward in Okene Local Government Area of Kogi State, announced his resignation from the ruling party in a letter addressed to the APC ward chairman. In the letter, made public on Tuesday, he said his resignation took immediate effect. He explained that the decision followed extensive consultations, careful consideration and an assessment of his political journey, personal convictions and future aspirations. Kareem said he had remained loyal and committed to the APC over the years, contributing his time, resources and efforts to the growth and development of the party. However, he said his decision to leave was informed by his belief that political participation should be based on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging. “I firmly believe that political participation should be anchored on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging,” he said. He expressed appreciation to the APC for the relationships he built and experiences gained during his membership, while wishing the party’s leadership well. Kareem’s defection to the PDP comes amid political realignments in Kogi Central ahead of future electoral contests. The post Kogi APC chieftain Kasco dumps party, joins PDP appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
items.description: The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday. CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028. The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final. The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year. “The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.” The host cities and other details will be announced later. “We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani. “We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.” The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Global hegemons and the discussion for peace: Negative peace, positive peace or economic peace?
items.description: The three world leaders, President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, on November 19, 2026, held a maiden edition of a tripartite engagement ostensibly to talk about peace. With the leaders declaring peace, will it be just a rhetoric or reality? Will these world leaders see to it that the negative peace concept is realized? Or will they empower international organizations such as the United Nations to facilitate positive peace in the global spectrum, where these three leaders play crucial roles in ensuring that the objective of negative peace is met? The United States of America, Russia, and China are all vetoes in the in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and known largest nuclear powers. What this means is that every decision taken outside of the UNSC needs to have cooperation among the individual states. With the meeting described as historic, the question is, what are the objective/s of these three leaders regarding what has been highlighted by the international media as a declaration for peace? The central conversation at the meeting was to commit to denuclearization and curb the consequences regarding nuclear proliferation. Will these leaders trust each other to the extent of limiting nuclear stockpiles? Or this meeting is one of those just for the optics? What is the uncertainty about? Russia is currently at war with Ukraine, USA is leading ‘military operations’ against Iran but China is not actively engaged in any armed conflict, but tensions remain in the South China Sea and around Taiwan. This is because China’s military drills and deployments, along with territorial disputes with India, Japan and Bhutan, make the situation in that region uncertain. With concrete actions taken by Russia and the USA regarding their role in the armed conflict in Ukraine and Iran, respectively, the lens is on China regarding what will happen next. Will China also exhibit tendencies as Russia and the USA, or will it really commit to peace as the meeting makes us to believe? Scholars, practitioners, and experts in the peace, security, and international relations field have questioned whether the actions of Russia, the USA, and China could be stopped. The United Nations (UN) has been accused of not enforcing its mandate to ensure international peace and security. This is due to the fact that the UN could not stop the actions of these states. If the UN could not stop the states from their current actions in the Middle East, Ukraine, and elsewhere, would they in the future when any states unilaterally violate international law? The uncertainty is also related to the fact that the President of the USA as the Chairman of the Board of Peace, together with Mr. Putin and Mr. Xi did not mention the specific target for which peace needs to be achieved. Self-interest or realism? These three global powers dominate the political and security landscape in their respective regions. The question arises if their actions amount to self-interest regarding how these leaders exhibit tendencies of power play and exert coercion in security. The ideal decision on the peace declaration would be to announce a vivid conviction regarding specificity in the commitment to peace and in the respective armed conflicts they are engaged in. The UN seem to be having a challenge regarding what to do, sanctions are not forthcoming. These leaders seem to take decisions at any given time without recourse to the effects on the global stage. Accusations are that, so far as these actions taken satisfies their national interest and satisfaction then it should be implemented. Regional organizations such as the European Union (EU), North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) are also watching events unfold whilst their opinions and suggestions are not considered. World peace seems to be at a crossroads at this moment, and the argument has been established that these three leaders have the authority to address the insecurities and resolve the conflicts for lasting peace to prevail. What does this mean for the Global South? We are economically interconnected. The Russia-Ukraine conflict gave us a glimpse of how worst we are ill-prepared for any global crises as a continent. As a result of the on-going conflict in the Middle East, fuel prices skyrocketed and the effects were felt at the pumps. When the pumps record high prices, it has rippling effects on every facet of the economy and that has been the story of most states in the Global South. The current Middle East armed conflict is protracting; we could continue to experience more economic and financial shocks in the micro and macro sectors of the economy. This can be addressed with the assistance of regional and sub-regional organizations such as the African Union (AU), the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), and Regional Economic Communities (RECs), respectively, implementing economic policies that will enable states to withstand any shock. Conclusion The power play is real, and unfortunately the rest of the world is at the receiving end of that power play and self-interest. In the name of sovereignty, some powerful states get away with wrongdoing, violate international laws and treaties. The values and norms on which international organizations such as the UN were established seem to be eroding because of the anarchy in the global governance spectrum. We need to be intentional and commit to peace. Peace is not just mere rhetoric but action. The absence of war is good, but if the structural variables that enable insecurity persist, we will end up with armed conflicts and not the absence of it. ****** Author: Doke, Victor PhD-Lecturer at GAFCSC

items.title: CSA calls for real-time communication platform to strengthen Ghana’s digital finance security
items.description: The Head of Cybersecurity Technology Standards at Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority (CSA), Jake France, has called for a real-time communications platform to enable banks, telecommunications companies, fintechs, regulators and other players in Ghana’s digital finance ecosystem share information on cyber incidents and emerging threats. The platform would help institutions alert one another quickly when breaches or fraudulent activities occur, allowing others in the ecosystem to assess their exposure and take appropriate action. The call reflects growing concerns that as digital financial services become increasingly interconnected, a security breach in one institution can have consequences for several others. “I believe a real-time communication platform which collates all the information for the sectors and the regulator to participate in is necessary,” he said, adding, “If we had one platform where all these institutions could report their breaches in real-time and we also had visibility of it, it would be easier to look at some of these issues and triage them in consultation with all the stakeholders. Unfortunately, we’re not there yet but that is the ultimate dream.” He cautioned that delays in reporting could expose more organisations to an attack because intelligence about a breach could not be disseminated quickly enough. A common platform, he stressed, should not serve as “a security camera looking at everybody’s transactions”, but as a means of rapidly communicating breaches and suspicious activity so institutions could assess their own environments and respond. He made the call during a UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC) and EY Ghana webinar on “Securing Ghana’s Digital Finance Ecosystem: From Institutional Silos to Building Collective Cyber Resilience.” The other panellists, including Elikplim Kitsikpui, Lead in EY Ghana’s Digital Technology Consulting team; Joy Aigbe, Head of Cybersecurity at Telecel Ghana; and John Awuah, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Association of Banks (GAB), supported the call, emphasising the need for stronger cooperation and faster information exchange among institutions. Kitsikpui said, “We can’t eliminate cybersecurity attacks, but we can minimise the impact. And to minimise that impact, we need to find a way of creating the platform that Jake spoke about.” Aigbe similarly prioritised “the establishment of a formal cross-sector cyber coordination and information-sharing platform” bringing together telcos, banks, fintechs, regulators, and relevant law-enforcement bodies. She said it must be operational, enabling participants to exchange intelligence, incident indicators, trends, and mitigation actions in near real time. John Awuah, in his support of the call, highlighted its urgency saying, “That platform, I can’t say enough that we need it like yesterday.” For Awuah, the urgency ultimately comes down to public confidence. “Trust, as we all see, is the currency of the digital finance system,” he remarked, arguing that once trust is compromised, the robustness of a system or the scale of investment in it means little to the customer. Collaboration key to preserving public trust For Aigbe, the growth of Ghana’s digital finance ecosystem has expanded financial inclusion while making institutions increasingly interdependent. This, she said, required a corresponding shift in how cybersecurity risks are managed. “The question is no longer whether an organisation can protect itself in isolation. The real measure of resilience is now how effectively the entire ecosystem can detect, communicate, and respond together when one part of the system comes under attack,” she said. She also recommended fraud operations centres within financial institutions to complement their security operations centres and serve as gateways for cross-institution collaboration. Kitsikpui stressed preparedness. Institutions, he said, should establish cross-institutional incident coordination frameworks, determine beforehand what information can be shared and with whom, define escalation thresholds, and test those arrangements jointly. “The middle of a cyber crisis is the wrong time to be identifying what to do, what to share, what not to share, and who to call,” he said. Awuah urged every participant to treat cyber risk with the same seriousness because an attack can rapidly cross institutional boundaries. “When there is a shared risk, what do you do? You need to have a shared response,” he said, calling for mechanisms that could detect attacks and trace or recover funds even after fraudulent proceeds had moved between banks and other platforms. The webinar, moderated by Traci Gyebi, a Technology Consultant at EY Ghana, also explored the role of banks and other financial-sector players in detecting, reporting and responding to fraud; emerging threats; customer education; third-party risks; coordinated incident response; and practical measures for building collective cyber resilience.

items.title: Camisetas, carteles y firmas: El ‘fenómeno fan’ por Rufián revoluciona la campaña de Esquerra
items.description: Un vídeo publicado en las redes sociales de Esquerra Republicana de Catalunya (ERC) en el que se promete regalar 200 camisetas ha sido el único toque de atención que el partido ha necesitado para atraer a centenares de personas frente a sus oficinas centrales en el Eixample (Barcelona). En el centro de la prenda, de un color naranja intenso, se erige un retrato bicolor del rostro de Gabriel Rufián, bajo el cual se lee el eslógan de la campaña del partido catalán: “Defensa’t” (’Defiéndete’). A las 16.30 h -media hora antes de la convocatoria oficial- la cola ya se alargaba más allá la esquina de la calle Sardenya por la Gran Via y, minutos más tarde, giraba la manzana hasta la calle Sicília. Los organizadores, sorprendidos ante semejante aglomeración, concuerdan al diagnosticar la clave de su éxito: es el factor Rufián. Seguir leyendo

Nigeria records 46,909 online abuse cases in one year
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Nigeria accounted for 58 per cent of verified online gender-based violence cases recorded across Africa in the last 12 months, with 46,909 incidents documented in the country, according to data from the OGBV Evidence Tracker. The figures were unveiled at a high-level consultative meeting on digital safety and online gender-based violence in schools, organised by the Centre for Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa (RACE Centre) under its Protect Secondary School Initiative in Abuja on Tuesday. Data from the tracker, powered by the RACE Centre, showed that 46,909 approved incidents were recorded between November 23, 2025, and November 23, 2026. The tracker monitors online abuse across Africa, with Nigeria recording the highest concentration of incidents with verified locations. X, formerly Twitter, accounted for 89 per cent of the documented cases, while Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube were also monitored. Harassment and general abuse topped the categories of violations, with 23,209 incidents, representing 56 per cent of the cases. Body shaming accounted for 7,662 incidents, representing 18 per cent, while slut shaming recorded 7,332 cases, also representing 18 per cent. Threats of violence accounted for 2,643 incidents, or six per cent. Other forms of abuse recorded included doxxing and privacy violations with 1,940 cases, synthetic artificial intelligence image manipulation with 1,730, stalking with 1,590 and impersonation with 790 incidents. The tracker had yet to publish a finalised report for November 2026 as the month was still ongoing, although its live dashboard indicated that the trend remained high. Speaking at the meeting, the Executive Director of RACE Centre, Evelyn Ugbe, said the organisation worked with feminist online watchers to document reports of abuse and refer victims to relevant authorities for intervention. “We have our feminist online watchers. When we get a report, we document and refer them to appropriate agencies such as NAPTIP, NSCDC and or the Police for immediate action,” she said. Ugbe urged parents to take a keen interest in their children’s online activities and create an enabling environment for teenagers to confide in them about their experiences in cyberspace. Stakeholders at the meeting said the figures highlighted the need for stronger accountability by digital platforms, improved digital safety education and faster responses to online abuse targeting women and girls. The meeting was attended by representatives of the Federal Ministry of Education, the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), civil society organisations and the media. items.title: CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title
items.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling that restored Senegal’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title following its dispute with Morocco. CAF made its position known in a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, saying it respected the decision of the Lausanne based tribunal and would take the necessary steps to give effect to it. “CAF respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it,” the football governing body said. The CAS ruling overturned the CAF Appeal Board’s decision of March 17, 2026, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after ruling that the Teranga Lions had forfeited the final. Instead, the tribunal reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board, which had upheld Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the final played in Rabat on January 18, 2026. The dispute followed a controversial incident late in regulation time when Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty. The Senegalese players returned after about 14 minutes, but Morocco captain Brahim Diaz failed to convert the spot kick. Senegal later secured victory through Pape Gueye’s goal in extra time. Morocco subsequently challenged the result, arguing that Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which address situations where a team abandons or refuses to continue a match. However, CAS ruled that the provisions did not apply because the referee had not permanently abandoned the match. The tribunal also held that the referee acted within his authority when he allowed play to resume. The decision was unanimous, according to CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb, who said the panel found no legal error in the referee’s handling of the incident. The tribunal’s ruling does not affect separate disciplinary sanctions imposed by CAF on Senegal coach Pape Thiaw and players Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr over incidents during the final. Although CAF has promised to comply with the decision, it has not yet provided details of the administrative steps or a timeline for implementing the ruling. CAS confirmed that the full grounds for its decision had been communicated to the parties on Tuesday. The award is expected to be made public in due course, unless the parties request that it remain confidential. The ruling brings an end to the dispute over the final and restores Senegal’s second AFCON title, following its first triumph in 2021. items.title: Retraite gouvernementale 2026 : Amadou Oury Bah lance la doctrine Mamadi Doumbouya, « la neutralité stratégique pour une stabilité durable »
items.description: La retraite gouvernementale 2026 a pris fin ce mardi 24 novembre à Maférinyah, dans la préfecture de Forécariah. À la clôture de trois jours de travaux, le Premier Ministre Amadou Oury Bah a annoncé le lancement de la doctrine Mamadi Doumbouya, intitulée « la neutralité stratégique pour une stabilité durable ». Une doctrine d'État fondée sur la souveraineté de la République, la primauté de l'intérêt national et la neutralité dans les rivalités des puissances. Réunis du 22 au 24 novembre à Maférinyah, sous la présidence du Premier Ministre Amadou Oury Bah, les membres du gouvernement guinéen et les préfets de la région de Kindia ont achevé ce mardi les travaux de la retraite gouvernementale 2026. À l'issue de cette rencontre consacrée à renforcer la cohésion, la coordination et l’efficacité de l’action gouvernementale, le chef du gouvernement a dressé le bilan des échanges et présenté les principales orientations retenues. Mais c'est surtout le lancement de la doctrine Mamadi Doumbouya qui a marqué cette cérémonie de clôture. Présentée comme une nouvelle boussole pour l'action de l'État, cette doctrine entend inscrire les décisions gouvernementales dans une vision durable, au-delà des urgences et des contraintes immédiates. Une retraite pour renforcer la solidarité gouvernementale Dans son discours, Amadou Oury Bah a d'abord exprimé sa « profonde reconnaissance » au Président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, dont il a salué la vision et la confiance accordée au gouvernement. « Sa vision fixe le cap de la nation. La confiance qu'il accorde au gouvernement nous oblige et c'est par les résultats que nous entendons l'honorer », a déclaré le Premier ministre. Il a également salué la mobilisation des conseillers de la présidence lors de la séance d'ouverture, avant de remercier les équipes de la Primature, du secrétariat général du gouvernement, les équipes techniques et logistiques ainsi que les autorités de Forécariah pour leur accueil. S'adressant aux Ministres, Amadou Oury Bah a salué leur participation à un exercice qu'il a qualifié de particulièrement exigeant pour une équipe gouvernementale : celui de soumettre les dossiers de chaque département à l'appréciation des autres membres du gouvernement. Selon lui, les ministres ont abordé cet exercice avec franchise et loyauté, permettant ainsi de mettre en évidence les interdépendances entre les différents départements. « Ces trois journées ont changé notre manière de travailler », a-t-il affirmé, estimant que le succès d'un ministère dépend également de l'action de ses collègues et de la collaboration avec les organismes chargés du suivi de l'exécution des projets. Le Premier ministre a ainsi souligné que les travaux ont permis de confronter, de hiérarchiser et d'orienter vers le règlement des questions jusque-là traitées de manière isolée par les administrations. Des blocages à examiner ministère par ministère À l'issue de cette retraite, Amadou Oury Bah a annoncé plusieurs mesures destinées à renforcer l'efficacité de l'action gouvernementale. Avant la fin de l'année 2026, les blocages affectant les projets de l'État seront passés en revue ministère par ministère. En 2027, le budget-programme devra lier chaque crédit à un responsable et à un résultat mesurable. Le chef du gouvernement a également insisté sur la nécessité d'assurer le suivi des instructions jusqu'à leur complète exécution. « Une exigence commune s'en dégage : celle d'un État qui prépare avant de s'engager. Cette exigence a désormais ses instruments », a-t-il indiqué. Dans cette dynamique, les lettres de mission devront, dès le début de l'année 2027, traduire les priorités communes du gouvernement en engagements précis assignés à chaque département ministériel. Le secrétariat général du gouvernement, en liaison avec le cabinet du Premier ministre, sera chargé d'en assurer le suivi. Amadou Oury Bah a, pour sa part, annoncé qu'il veillerait personnellement à ce que tout blocage porté à sa connaissance reçoive un arbitrage. L'approbation du programme économique et financier par le FMI Le Premier ministre a également évoqué l'approbation, le lundi 23 novembre, par le conseil d'administration du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), du programme économique et financier de la République de Guinée pour la période 2026-2029. Il a présenté cette décision comme une reconnaissance des réformes engagées par le gouvernement et du travail accompli par les différentes équipes. « Cette décision ne doit rien au hasard. Elle est le fruit des réformes que nous avons engagées et du travail patient de l'ensemble des équipes que je félicite », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Amadou Oury Bah, cette approbation constitue un résultat qui doit désormais ouvrir la voie à d'autres avancées concrètes, perceptibles dans la vie quotidienne des Guinéens. « Nos compatriotes attendent des résultats et voici un. Il nous oblige à en produire d'autres que chaque Guinéen puisse constater dans sa vie quotidienne », a-t-il souligné. La doctrine Mamadi Doumbouya, une boussole pour l'action de l'État Au-delà des questions de coordination et de suivi des projets, le discours de clôture a été marqué par le lancement de la doctrine Mamadi Doumbouya : « la neutralité stratégique pour une stabilité durable ». Pour présenter cette doctrine, Amadou Oury Bah a d'abord rappelé les héritages historiques et culturels des quatre régions naturelles de la Guinée, qu'il considère comme les fondements d'une mémoire commune. La Haute-Guinée, a-t-il expliqué, a apporté à la nation la profondeur du Manding et le droit porté par la parole. Le Fouta lui a légué l'autorité du savoir et l'art des institutions. La Basse-Guinée, présentée comme la porte atlantique du pays, lui a appris à s'ouvrir au monde sans se soumettre. Quant à la Guinée forestière, elle lui a transmis la force de ses sociétés et la solidarité dans l'épreuve. Le Premier ministre a également rappelé que les routes de la cola, du sel et de l'or reliaient ces territoires bien avant la naissance de la nation guinéenne. « Ces quatre héritages sont les affluents d'un même fleuve et leur rencontre a rendu possible le choix de 1958 », a-t-il déclaré. De cette mémoire commune découle, selon lui, une doctrine d'État qui doit désormais servir de référence aux décisions publiques. Souveraineté, intérêt national et neutralité stratégique Dans sa présentation, Amadou Oury Bah a défini les principaux fondements de cette doctrine : la souveraineté de la République, la primauté de l'intérêt national et la neutralité dans les rivalités des puissances. Cette orientation doit permettre à la Guinée de : « traiter avec tous sans dépendre d'aucun », a-t-il affirmé. Le chef du gouvernement a également souligné que cette doctrine entend orienter les ressources nationales vers la transformation de l'économie et l'élévation des populations. L'objectif, selon lui, est de faire en sorte que la dignité portée par le choix de 1958 s'accomplisse dans la prospérité, dont le programme Simandou 2040 trace le chemin. « Cette doctrine guidera désormais nos décisions et orientera notre action », a insisté le Premier ministre. Il a précisé que chaque ministre devra y trouver sa feuille de route, chaque serviteur de l'État sa règle de conduite et chaque citoyen une raison de fierté. Au terme de son intervention, Amadou Oury Bah a officiellement déclaré clos les travaux de la retraite gouvernementale 2026, avant de procéder au lancement de la doctrine Mamadi Doumbouya, « la neutralité stratégique pour une stabilité durable ». Une annonce qui place désormais cette doctrine au cœur des orientations présentées par le gouvernement à l'issue de ces trois jours de travaux à Maférinyah. items.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. items.title: GBV costs Nigeria $3bn annually – Minister
items.description: …Over 27,000 cases of sexual, gender-based violence documented . ..ActionAid calls for stronger law enforcement to end GBV By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, has said gender-based violence (GBV) costs Nigeria about $3 billion annually, representing approximately 1.5 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Sulaiman-Ibrahim disclosed this in Abuja on Monday during a press briefing to mark the commencement of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence. She said the economic and social consequences of GBV included loss of productivity, physical deformities, depression, healthcare challenges, family breakdown, school dropouts and job losses. The minister also disclosed that more than 27,000 cases of sexual and gender-based violence were documented in the most recent reporting cycle, warning that millions of cases remained unreported. She said one in three Nigerian women aged 15 to 49 had experienced physical or sexual violence. According to her, the trauma suffered by survivors is often compounded by societal stigma, which leaves many battling low self-esteem and other psychological consequences. She called for concerted efforts by government and non-state actors to provide support and assistance to survivors. “We cannot afford to merely count these numbers. We must turn remembrance into rescue,” she said. The minister said her ministry was collaborating with state governments to establish sexual assault referral centres in every local government area to improve access to support services at the grassroots. She added that the government was also pursuing a vision of establishing sexual assault centres in every ward under the Union of Social Impact Intervention. Sulaiman-Ibrahim commended development partners, including the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), UNICEF, World Bank, Spring Projects, Ideas International, WaterAid, ActionAid, Policy Innovation Centre, Save the Children, Women at Risk International Foundation and Safe Jobmas, for their contributions to efforts against GBV. Meanwhile, the Country Director of ActionAid Nigeria, Andrew Mamedu, represented by the organisation’s Women’s Rights Specialist, Niri Goyit, described gender-based violence as a grave human rights violation that continues to undermine the dignity, safety and opportunities of millions of women and girls. Citing findings from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, Mamedu said 21 per cent of women aged 15 to 49 had experienced physical or sexual violence, while 23 per cent of ever-married or partnered women had experienced physical, sexual or emotional violence from their current or most recent partners. He stressed that ending GBV required effective implementation of existing laws, adequately funded survivor-support services, accessible justice systems and accountability for perpetrators, regardless of their status or influence. Speaking on the 2026 16 Days of Activism theme, ‘UNiTE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity’, he called on federal and state governments, security agencies, justice institutions, civil society organisations, development partners, the media and community leaders to translate commitments into measurable action. He urged governments and relevant institutions to strengthen enforcement of the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act and other protective legal frameworks, close implementation gaps and invest in safe, accessible and survivor-centred services. Mamedu also called for measures to ensure that every woman and girl could access justice, irrespective of her location or socioeconomic circumstances. Also speaking, the UNFPA Resident Representative in Nigeria, Ms. Muriel Mafico, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to ending sexual and gender-based violence, with the message: “Name it. Believe it. End it.” She said violence that remained unnamed often went unaddressed, describing the identification of all forms of GBV as a critical first step towards justice and prevention. “Violence against women and girls must never be normalised, excused or concealed. Whether it occurs in our homes, communities, institutions or digital spaces, every survivor deserves to be heard, protected, and supported to access justice,” Mafico said. items.title: “My mission remains to put the people first in the development of Akuapem” – Sammi Awuku
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Akuapem North, Sammi Awuku, Esq., has reiterated his commitment to ensure he drives the development of his constituency with a focus on the welfare of the people of the area. He says this remains his focus, and he is committed to investing into the people of Akuapem North so that development of the area will be felt by all. “Our mission remains to put the people first and ensure that development is not just seen but felt by everyone because development must reach every community in Akuapem North Constituency”, he stated. This is after the legislator had presented cheques to some constituents to support their welfare. “The day also saw cheques presentations to 45 constituents to support their businesses, education and healthcare needs, alongside scholarship support for deserving beneficiaries,” he wrote on his Facebook page. Sammi Awuku also hosted students from Akropong Practice Basic School who went to invite the MP, regarded by many constituents as a best performing Legislator to homecoming celebration. “Another productive and inspiring day in Akuapem North! I was delighted to welcome the Girls’ Prefect of Akropong Practice Basic School and her colleagues to my office at Mamfe. “Beyond their invitation to their upcoming Homecoming celebration, we had an engaging conversation about their dreams and how I can support their aspirations. I was particularly excited to hear the Girls’ Prefect speak about her ambition of becoming a lawyer and someday, Ghana’s Minister for Education,” he wrote.

items.title: Borno police warn of road closures ahead of Tinubu’s visit
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Borno State Police Command has warned motorists and residents of possible temporary closures of major roads in Maiduguri ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s visit to the state on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. The visit is expected to coincide with the launch of the President’s 2027 re-election campaign. The Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Kenneth Daso, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the temporary restrictions would be part of security arrangements for the presidential visit and other Very Important Personalities expected in the state. According to him, some major roads and adjoining routes within the metropolis may be temporarily closed to vehicular movement to facilitate security operations and ensure the smooth conduct of the visit. “Motorists, commuters and other road users are advised to plan their journeys accordingly,” Daso said. He added that alternative routes would be provided and communicated to the public to ease movement during the period. The police spokesman also urged residents to comply with traffic regulations and directives from security personnel, while soliciting the understanding and cooperation of the public over any inconvenience caused by the restrictions. Our correspondent reports that heightened security measures have often accompanied presidential visits to Borno State since the outbreak of the Boko Haram insurgency in 2009. Such measures, including traffic restrictions and road closures, have sometimes attracted complaints from residents over the disruption of movement and daily economic activities. items.title: FIFM : Conversation avec James Gray, leçon de cinéma sans filtre et à cœur ouvert
items.description: Invité des « Conversations » du Festival International du Film de Marrakech face au directeur de la Mostra de Venise Alberto Barbera, le cinéaste américain James Gray, qui a présenté son nouveau film Paper Tiger, a livré une leçon de cinéma aussi drôle que lumineuse. Des cinémas de répertoire de New York aux coulisses mouvementées de ses tournages avec Brad Pitt ou Anthony Hopkins, retour sur la masterclass d'un auteur qui refuse l'ironie au profit de l'émotion pure. Avec seulement neuf longs-métrages en trente-deux ans de carrière, James Gray, qui en a d'ailleurs plaisanté face au public de Marrakech, fait figure d'exception dans le paysage cinématographique américain. Accueilli sous les applaudissements, le réalisateur new-yorkais a d’emblée donné le ton : sincère, autodérisoire et profondément passionné. Rien ne prédestinait pourtant ce fils d'un ingénieur et d'une enseignante du Queens, issue d'un milieu ouvrier sans aucun lien avec le monde artistique, à passer derrière la caméra. Le déclic survient à l'âge de 10 ans, lorsque son père l’emmène par hasard voir Apocalypse Now au Ziegfeld Theatre de New York. « Un acte de pure folie parentale » , s'amuse le cinéaste, qui se souvient avoir été fasciné par ce mystère sonore et visuel avant d'être définitivement converti l'année suivante par Raging Bull de Martin Scorsese. Contre l'avis de sa mère, qui lui prédisait l'échec faute de relations, le jeune homme forge son regard dans les salles de répertoire miteuses de Times Square et devant les toiles d'Edward Hopper. Son entrée dans le cinéma en 1994 avec Little Odessa , tourné à seulement 23 ans, relève cependant du parcours du combattant. Jugé trop sombre par son studio, New Line, le film est menacé d'être mis au placard jusqu'à un coup de fil salvateur de Gillo Pontecorvo, alors directeur de la Mostra de Venise, qui qualifie l'œuvre de chef-d'œuvre. Persuadé que sa carrière est finie, le jeune cinéaste reprend l'avion pour Los Angeles, avant d'être rattrapé sur la passerelle de l'aéroport : le jury présidé par David Lynch vient de lui décerner le Lion d'argent. « David Lynch a littéralement sauvé ma carrière » , résumé-t-il. Interrogé par Alberto Barbera sur la place centrale de la famille dans son œuvre, James Gray convoque aussi bien la tragédie grecque qu'Eugene O'Neill. Pour lui, le véritable moteur dramaturgique n'est pas l'affrontement spectaculaire, mais le conflit intérieur : « Comment suis-je en guerre avec moi-même ? » La cellule familiale est l'espace où cohabitent à parts égales l'amour le plus pur et l'angoisse la plus vive. C'est précisément cette vulnérabilité que l'art permet de partager : « Vous vous réveillez à 4 heures du matin et vous pensez : je suis seul au monde. L'art est notre salut, parce qu'il nous dit q ue notre angoisse n'est pas unique. » Mounir Mehimdate Des fonds verts d'Ad Astra à l'intime d'Armageddon Time Le cinéaste n'a pas éludé les zones d'ombre de sa filmographie, évoquant la frustration du tournage d' Ad Astra (2019). Malgré l'inventivité et les improvisations remarquables de Brad Pitt, James Gray décrit l'épreuve de diriger un acteur « suspendu à des câbles dans une boîte verte pendant quinze heures par jour » , tout en déplorant la perte de son final cut suite au rachat de la Fox par Disney. « Quand vous préparez une sauce, vous n'avez pas envie qu'un inconnu entre dans la cuisine pour y ajouter du cumin » , lance-t-il à son interlocuteur italien. En réaction à cette superproduction, il tourne en 2022 Armageddon Time , plongée autobiographique dans son enfance. Pour éviter le piège d'un récit limité au regard moral d'un garçon de 11 ans, il confie le rôle du grand-père à Anthony Hopkins, véritable « pivot moral » du film, saluant un acteur « incapable du moindre instant inauthentique » . « C'est un signe clair, car j'ai réalisé un film très sombre sur mon enfance, totalement autobiographique, et ils m'ont laissé faire. C'est incroyable. Le film est dur, vraiment sombre, et je ne sais pas trop comment j'ai pu le réaliser, mais je me sens très privilégié, vraiment. Et puis, j'ai la chance d'avoir des acteurs aussi formidable » , a-t-il déclaré. En conclusion de cet échange, lorsqu'Alberto Barbera évoque la dimension « mélodramatique » de son cinéma, notamment dans son nouveau film Paper Tiger , irrité par la musique de Puccini , James Gray nuance avec élégance. S'il admire Douglas Sirk, il préfère revendiquer l'héritage de l'opéra. Contrairement à l'air du temps qui privilégie la déconstruction et la distance ironique, l'opéra exige une adhésion totale : « Le créateur ne peut pas se placer au-dessus de son œuvre. Nous avons besoin du fantasme des émotions pour survivre. » Une profession de foi vibrante pour un cinéma qui, loin de tout cynisme, continue de viser droit au cœur. The post FIFM : Conversation avec James Gray, leçon de cinéma sans filtre et à cœur ouvert appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in the Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area of the state. The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, was arrested following reports of repeated grave desecration at the cemetery. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the arrest followed a surveillance operation mounted by the police in collaboration with concerned youths in the community. According to him, on November 10, 2026, at about 7:15 p.m., shortly after the burial of a deceased person, the suspect was allegedly caught digging into the newly covered grave. Usman said vigilant youths apprehended him while he was allegedly committing the act and immediately alerted the police. He added that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons. The police spokesman further said the suspect reportedly admitted involvement in previous acts of grave desecration at the same cemetery, including an earlier incident in which he allegedly removed and took away the burial shroud of a deceased person. Usman said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action. The command commended members of the community for their vigilance and cooperation, while cautioning residents against taking the law into their own hands. It urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities to the police. The post Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN 2025 : Le TAS annule la décision de la CAF et rétablit officiellement le Sénégal comme champion d’Afrique
items.description: Le Sénégal retrouve officiellement son titre de champion d’Afrique 2025. Sa victoire 1-0 en prolongation lors de la finale de la CAN 2025 face au Maroc a été homologuée, infirmant ainsi la décision de forfait prononcée par le jury d’appel de la CAF. Le Tribunal arbitral du sport a admis à l’unanimité, ce 24 novembre 2026 à Lausanne, l’appel de la Fédération sénégalaise de football. Le Sénégal est redevenu champion d’Afrique. Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) s’est appuyé sur la souveraineté de l’arbitre et sur la loi 5 du jeu de l’IFAB (Conseil international du football association) pour désigner le Sénégal champion d’Afrique 2025. Le jury du TAS a admis à l’unanimité l’appel de la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF). Il a annulé la décision du jury d’appel de la CAF du 17 mars 2026 (NDLR : le jury d’appel de la CAF avait déclaré le Sénégal perdant par forfait, 3-0 sur tapis vert contre le Maroc, à la suite du retrait temporaire de ses joueurs lors de la finale du 18 janvier 2026 à Rabat) et rétabli le Sénégal comme champion d’Afrique 2025. Le résultat acquis sur le terrain, 1-0 en prolongation en faveur du Sénégal, est homologué, ce qui confère aux Lions de la Teranga leur deuxième titre continental. Le TAS fonde sa décision sur la souveraineté de l’arbitre sur le terrain. La doctrine du terrain de jeu confère une autorité exclusive à l’arbitre, conformément à la loi 5 du jeu. Cette loi, éditée par l’IFAB, stipule que les décisions de l’arbitre sur des faits en relation avec le jeu sont définitives, y compris la validation d’un but et le résultat du match. « Après avoir examiné les arguments exposés par les parties, le Tribunal arbitral du sport a considéré que la décision de l’arbitre de reprendre ou d’arrêter le match était de sa seule responsabilité. En relançant le match, l’arbitre a considéré que les conditions pour reprendre le match étaient réunies, les deux équipes étant à nouveau sur le terrain et ayant exprimé leur volonté de reprendre », a expliqué le TAS dans son communiqué. Le TAS estime qu’il n’y a aucune erreur de droit ou d’arbitrage. Il a précisé que l’arbitre est le seul juge du bon déroulement du match, qu’il disposait de l’autorité exclusive pour décider si le match était définitivement arrêté ou si les conditions étaient réunies pour qu’il reprenne et que, dès lors qu’il a sifflé la reprise sans erreur de droit ni d’arbitrage, les instances disciplinaires ne pouvaient remettre en cause la poursuite de la rencontre. La sentence complète du TAS, détaillant l’ensemble des motifs juridiques à l’issue de l’audience tenue le 8 octobre 2026 à Lausanne, a été notifiée aux parties ce mardi 24 novembre 2026. Faso7 L’article CAN 2025 : Le TAS annule la décision de la CAF et rétablit officiellement le Sénégal comme champion d’Afrique est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Huang’s return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
items.description: Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as caution returned after Jensen Huang’s extraordinary return to AI giant Nvidia days after he was forced to resign, with investors bracing for further volatility in a key sector driving economic growth worldwide. A day after Huang’s reinstatement as CEO drove Nvidia shares up more than 30 per cent, adding more than $900 billion to the firm’s market value, the euphoria dissipated as its stock lost almost 9pc mid-session. Fellow tech behemoth and AI giant Anthropic also slumped, giving up around 12pc to $77.19, below its $83 price for last week’s IPO. Monday aside, AI stocks had already sold off sharply throughout November on worries about profitability and the vast sums pumped into the sector. Overall, the tech-heavy Nasdaq shed 2.3pc and the broader-based S&P 500 lost 1.1pc, while the Dow was just into the green around 1700 GMT (10pm PKT). Europe’s main stock markets, which feature far fewer tech companies than their Asian and US rivals, finished a handful of percentage points lower after jumping on Monday in line with Wall Street. Away from the tech sector, French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi revealed it would buy the US biopharma group Insmed, a specialist in respiratory treatments, for $41bn as it races to bulk up its development pipeline of new drugs. Sanofi’s share price closed up almost 10pc following the news. Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago over extramarital affairs, reportedly with an alleged Chinese spy as well as a senior Nvidia executive before US President Donald Trump noisily declared he should be brought back. “Jensen’s return takes away one of the biggest unknowns hanging over the AI trade,” said Charu Chanana, an investment strategist at Saxo Markets. “He is not just Nvidia’s CEO; he is arguably the biggest salesman for the entire AI ecosystem. His relationships with customers, suppliers and capital providers are difficult to replicate,” she said. But “Jensen Huang alone cannot support the AI trade in the long term,” said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. “Nvidia’s stock price decline on Tuesday is to be expected after such a large rally in the previous session,” she added. Analysts were in broad agreement that Huang’s return did not mean an end to probes or the uncertainty that has clouded the AI trade for six months. The company remains under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips. Monday’s Wall Street surge had propelled Asian markets earlier on Tuesday, with Taipei surging 9pc higher as chip titans TSMC and MediaTek added nearly 10pc each. Seoul piled on more than 6pc thanks to strong gains in fellow chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung, and Tokyo rose nearly 4pc, led by a 12.5pc jump for semiconductor tester Advantest.

items.title: Tension flares again at Suame Magazine as artisans resist move to reopen locked shops
items.description: Tension has flared up again at Suame Magazine after artisans resisted attempts by National Security personnel to reopen shops locked during an earlier confrontation between Ghanaian traders and foreign spare-parts dealers. The latest standoff comes despite a meeting between the National Security Council and the Ghana Union of Traders Associations (GUTA), which was expected to pave the way for the reopening of the affected shops. Captain Jabari said GUTA had agreed to reopen the affected shops before 12 noon on Tuesday. He explained that security officials would visit the facility to engage the artisans and other stakeholders before meeting Nigerian representatives to clarify the business activities permitted at the Magazine. “We’ll be going to the Magazine to have a stakeholder engagement with them. Then from there, we’ll have another meeting with the Nigerian counterparts on what they can and cannot do at the Magazine. So GUTA has decided on its own to open up the shops that they locked up yesterday before 12 o’clock,” he said. Read also: Suame Magazine artisans ordered to reopen shops of Nigerian spare-parts dealers The security agencies also assured traders that laws governing foreign participation in Ghana’s retail sector will be enforced. However, when security personnel moved in this evening to enforce the directive, some artisans met them with stiff resistance, leading to a tense confrontation. The renewed confrontation has heightened concerns over the growing tension between local artisans, foreign spare-parts dealers and security personnel at the enclave.

items.title: Sputnik-S, el satélite ruso que amenaza con llevar la guerra nuclear al espacio
items.description: Los servicios de inteligencia de Estados Unidos revelaron por primera vez hace tres años que Rusia estaba diseñando un satélite equipado con una carga nuclear. Desde 2023 ha habido tiempo para desarrollar el Sputnik-S y en este momento fuentes militares y de los servicios secretos alemanes sostienen que el aparato está listo para ser colocado en órbita dentro de dos meses. La lógica militar es evidente: Ucrania puede desde 2022 defenderse de la invasión rusa gracias a la red de satélites Starlink o las imágenes que toman desde el espacio sus aliados de la OTAN. items.title: Suspect linked to seven rape and robbery cases dies during Kade police operation
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has linked a 39-year-old ex-convict, Kwaku Asomani, to seven cases of robbery and rape, as well as the murder of a 28-year-old woman in Kade and surrounding communities in the Kwaebibirem District of the Eastern Region. The Eastern South Regional Police Command said preliminary investigations implicated Asomani in seven separate incidents involving female victims between February 19 and November 10, 2026. According to the police, the suspect targeted women aged between 18 and 54, robbing them of various sums of money and personal belongings before sexually assaulting them. Investigations also linked him to the death of Esther Opoku, 28, whose body was discovered on October 1, 2026, opposite Hotel De Nyarko in the Guggisberg area of Kade. The breakthrough followed intensive surveillance operations by investigators from the Anti-Armed Robbery Unit of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) Headquarters, working in collaboration with personnel of the Kade District Command. The police said the team located Asomani on November 14, 2026, at Assemblies of God in Kade during an operation in which he sustained gunshot wounds and subsequently died. A search of his person and residence led to the retrieval of a face cap and other clothing items, which some of the victims have reportedly identified as belonging to the suspect. The Eastern South Regional Police Command has expressed sympathy to the family of Esther Opoku and said arrangements were being made to provide psychosocial support to the surviving victims. The Command also reaffirmed the Ghana Police Service’s commitment to combating violent crime and protecting lives and property, assuring residents of its continued efforts to ensure public safety.

items.title: Et de deux !
items.description: «Ô temps, suspends ton vol, et vous, heures propices, suspendez votre cours !» Dans Le Lac, publié en 1820 dans ses Méditations poétiques, Alphonse de Lamartine exprime l’impuissance de l’homme face au temps qui emporte les instants heureux. Bouleversé par la disparition d’un bonheur qu’il voudrait éternel, le poète implore le temps de retenir ce qui, déjà, appartient au souvenir. Près de deux siècles plus tard, ces vers trouvent une résonance particulière dans l’histoire récente du football sénégalais. La finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations du 18 janvier 2026, à Rabat, marque au-delà du cadre d’une compétition sportive. Elle est entrée dans la mémoire collective d’un peuple. Ce soir-là, le Sénégal cherchait une deuxième étoile, quatre ans après son premier sacre au Cameroun. Le Maroc, porté par son public, espérait renouer avec un titre continental qui lui échappait depuis 1976. Au terme d’une rencontre sous haute tension, la finale bascula dans une séquence tumultueuse. Un but sénégalais refusé, un penalty accordé aux Marocains après intervention de la VAR, une vive contestation et une interruption du match. Les Lions quittèrent momentanément la pelouse avant d’y revenir. Puis Brahim Díaz manqua sa panenka face à Édouard Mendy. Le sort de la rencontre allait finalement se jouer en prolongation. À la 94e minute, Pape Gueye inscrit un but magistral face à Yassine Bounou. Le Sénégal prit l’avantage et ne le lâcha plus. Au coup de sifflet final, tout le pays jusque dans les coins les plus reculés vibrent à l’unisson. Drapeaux, klaxons et scènes de liesse accompagnèrent cette deuxième consécration continentale, vécue comme une immense délivrance nationale. Comment effacer une telle émotion ? Cette joie a été éprouvée dans les tribunes, devant les écrans, dans les familles et jusque dans les rues. Elle appartient désormais à la mémoire collective du Sénégal. La loi du sport, dans toute sa grandeur La grandeur du sport réside aussi dans sa capacité à susciter des émotions qui traversent les générations. Ce soir-là, la joie sénégalaise avait hélas engendrait la désolation marocaine. C’est aussi la loi du sport. L’espérance des uns se nourrit parfois de la déception des autres. Depuis, cette finale a quitté le seul terrain sportif pour celui des procédures. Le 17 mars 2026, le jury d’appel de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a déclaré le Sénégal forfait et attribué la victoire au Maroc sur le score de 3-0. La Fédération sénégalaise de football a saisi le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) pour contester cette décision. L’instance de Lausanne a rendu sa sentence ce 24 novembre. Il importe toutefois de distinguer le contentieux juridique de la mémoire du match. Les instances compétentes ont vocation à statuer sur les règlements et leurs conséquences. Mais aucune procédure ne peut effacer les émotions vécues, les images gravées dans les consciences ou la communion d’un peuple autour d’un événement. La décision du TAS appartient à l’histoire du droit sportif. Mais, cette nuit du 18 janvier a déjà sa place dans le cœur du peuple Sénégalais. On peut contester un résultat, discuter une décision et prolonger un contentieux. On ne peut retirer à un peuple le bonheur qu’il a réellement vécu. Certaines émotions résistent au temps et aux controverses. Pour le Sénégal, cette soirée restera à jamais ancrée. Une nuit que la mémoire nationale n’est pas prête de laisser s’effacer. O.BA
