items.title: Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, life jackets and other water safety equipment to riverine communities in Bayelsa State following a deadly boat mishap. The House also urged relevant agencies to intensify rescue operations, provide relief materials to affected communities and investigate the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Rodney Ebikebina Ambaiowei, representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, during plenary on Tuesday. Ambaiowei told the House that more than 150 people, mostly indigenes of Southern Ijaw, were involved in the accident on November 20, 2026, while travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a condolence visit. He said the boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan, throwing its occupants into the water. According to him, rescue efforts began immediately, with the Bayelsa State Government, security personnel and other relevant agencies responding to the incident. He disclosed that, as of November 22, several people had been rescued alive with varying degrees of injuries and discomfort, while others had died. The rescued victims, he said, were taken to medical facilities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area and government hospitals in Yenagoa for treatment, while search and rescue operations continued for missing persons and possible survivors. The lawmaker expressed concern that several victims were still missing, despite the efforts of the state government, and called for a broader search operation. He said the tragedy had plunged families and residents of Southern Ijaw, particularly Ukubie and neighbouring communities, into mourning. Ambaiowei attributed the vulnerability of riverine communities partly to the poor condition of boats used for transportation, noting that many were old, overworked and overloaded because of the scarcity of vessels. He also lamented the absence of life jackets, floaters and other water safety equipment, as well as inadequate enforcement of their use, despite waterways being the major means of transportation in the largely riverine constituency. The lawmaker said the communities had limited access to motorable roads, despite ongoing road construction efforts by the Bayelsa State Government, leaving residents heavily dependent on waterways. He warned that failure by the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant bodies to intensify rescue operations and provide relief materials could worsen the impact of the tragedy. Ambaiowei added that the affected communities depended largely on fishing for food and income, stressing that the accident had disrupted their livelihoods and economic activities. He commended President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the affected area to sympathise with families of the deceased. The lawmaker also acknowledged the Federal Government’s donation of ₦250 million to victims of the tragedy. Contributions to the motion centred on the need for safer water transportation, stricter enforcement of safety standards and accountability by government agencies and community-level authorities. House Minority Leader, Rep. Fred Agbedi, said the accident had exposed the hardship faced by riverine communities, arguing that government transportation interventions had largely overlooked people who depended on waterways. Agbedi advocated the provision of modern boats at subsidised rates, similar to the Federal Government’s introduction of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses to reduce the cost of road transportation. “Mr Speaker, this happening brings to attention what the people of the riverine communities are suffering. And I think it’s a moment that we should use to also assuage the challenges. “I’m aware that the federal government is providing CNG buses, you know, that are more economical. But each time we talk about mass transit and all that, there is no river craft provision. “So in this century, you see people using a dugout boat, you know, with weak roofs, that will collapse from the roof on the people who are sitting at the bottom. If government has provided, as we do mass transit and do CNG buses and all that, if vessels are provided for transportation at subsidised rates, I’m sure that this incident will have been averted,” he said. Agbedi described the motion as an opportunity to address the longstanding neglect of riverine communities, insisting that federal transportation policies should also cater for people with little or no access to roads. He urged the Federal Government to make budgetary provisions for modern and affordable boats, alongside its planned interventions in road transportation. Rep. Shina Oyedeji urged the government to stop paying lip service to safety standards, saying the tragedy should serve as a wake-up call for authorities to regulate transportation operations properly. He questioned the training and certification of boat operators and the standards governing the use of boats and other transport facilities. Oyedeji also called for a review of safety procedures and certification requirements, insisting that operators must be properly trained and qualified. “We cannot continue to assume that they do it in America, they do it in the UK, they do it in Russia or Morocco, we want to do it here without having the right process. We must write a manner that can say this is how it must be done,” he said. He urged the relevant committee of the House to examine the country’s safety standards and ensure that necessary regulations were enforced. The Deputy Majority Whip, Rep. Isiaka Ibrahim, said responsibility for safety on inland waterways rested with both the Federal and state governments, noting that creeks and offshore waters were on the concurrent legislative list. He urged the House to investigate the accident and examine the safety practices of operators, particularly in comparison with those of multinational companies operating offshore. Ibrahim argued that adopting even a fraction of the safety measures observed by multinational companies could help prevent accidents in the creeks. He also warned against disregarding life jackets on the assumption that swimming ability could guarantee survival in an accident. “I know how to swim. I have been swimming for 40 years. No, you don’t even know the condition of the boat or the condition of the water or the depth or what may have happened to the boat. “Life vests, life jackets, we ignore it. And then we are not talking about mishap. Definitely, it’s a hazard,” he said. He urged the House to use the incident as a learning opportunity and address the circumstances that led to the tragedy. House Leader, Rep. Julius Ihonvbere, however, stressed the need to hold grassroots authorities and community organisations accountable for safety failures. He said footage from the accident showed people boarding boats without life jackets, describing the practice as unacceptable and calling for tougher penalties against those who violated safety regulations. Ihonvbere argued that community associations, maritime associations, local government councils, state governments and relevant agencies all had responsibilities to ensure safety on waterways. He insisted that familiarity with waterways or swimming experience should not be used as an excuse for ignoring safety requirements. “The fact that I was born in the river side, I was thrown into the river, I was a baby, I have been swimming for 20, 35 years, is not an excuse to board a boat without the appropriate life vest,” he said. He also questioned the inspection of watercraft and called for stronger enforcement of safety regulations at jetties and other boarding points. Ihonvbere said recurring accidents would continue unless authorities at all levels took responsibility and imposed appropriate penalties for safety violations. The House unanimously adopted the motion and mandated its Committee on Emergency and Disaster Management to work with NEMA and the Bayelsa State Government to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and recommend measures to prevent future occurrences. It also called on NEMA, the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), the National Inland Waterways Authority and the South-South Development Agency to provide additional relief materials to affected communities to cushion the impact of the tragedy and the loss of livelihoods. The House further urged the agencies to urgently supply safer boats, life jackets, floaters and other water transport safety equipment to riverine communities, while ensuring their mandatory use. The post Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « D’ici 2030, nous avons l’ambition d’aller vers 400 millions de flux vidéo annualisés en données agricoles »
items.description: Aller vers 400 millions de flux vidéo annualisés en données agricoles et en données d'irrigation d'ici 2030, c’est ce que veulent les créateurs de Sotilma. Une startup sénégalaise qui propose des équipements digitalisés et une IA capable et accessible sur WhatsApp, en wolof et en français, qui permet aux agriculteurs de pouvoir gérer leurs fermes à distance en restant chez eux. C’est ce qu’a indiqué Adja Aminata Cissé Diop, directrice générale et cofondatrice de Sotilma, lors d’un entretien mardi, à l’occasion de Demo Day organisé lors de la cérémonie de clôture du programme d’incubation de la cohorte IA, deeptech et géospatial 2026. Vous êtes une des bénéficiaires du programme Goin’ Digital. Pouvez-vous revenir sur la particularité de cette initiative ? Nous sommes les bénéficiaires du programme Goin’ Digital et cela a été un immense plaisir pour nous de participer à ce programme. On a l'habitude de voir que l'accompagnement pour les solutions IA c'est d'habitude à la base technique. Donc aujourd'hui avec Goin’ Digital, on n'a pas eu qu'un accompagnement technique. mais on a surtout eu un accompagnement en termes de ressources humaines et surtout en formation. Ils nous ont mis en relation avec des institutions qui parfois sont difficiles d'accès pour les startups ou les jeunes startups locales. Et nous avons eu cette possibilité-là avec Goin’ Digital de passer de la vente d'équipements, du développement de notre IA à une IA accessible qu'on compte lancer ce 1ᵉʳ décembre 2026. On a déjà des IA qui sont dans le domaine de l'agriculture, aujourd'hui quelle est la différence avec ce que vous offrez ? Alors il faut savoir que les défis majeurs de l'agriculture aujourd'hui au Sénégal, sont essentiellement au nombre de quatre. Il y a la surveillance limitée, les outils dispersés, une irrigation qui est mal optimisée et surtout et en plus des technologies qui sont surtout inadaptées aux réalités de notre terrain. A lire aussi : Leadership féminin: l’accès au numérique, un accélérateur d’opportunités Aujourd'hui ce que nous proposons, c'est une IA qui est directement accessible par un outil que les agriculteurs utilisent déjà, ils n'ont pas besoin de télécharger une nouvelle application, pas besoin d'interface compliquée, pas besoin de savoir lire ou écrire, ils utilisent juste leur WhatsApp et aujourd'hui ils ont la possibilité d'avoir toutes ces applications réunies sur leur WhatsApp. Ils ont la capacité aujourd'hui d'avoir le rapport journalier de tout ce qui se passe dans leur ferme dans les 48 h, 24 h, 72 h, ça dépend d'eux. Ils ont la capacité d'allumer et de fermer leur van, leur pompe, tout leur système d'irrigation. Ils ont la capacité avec le WhatsApp aussi d'avoir des recommandations personnalisées sur les types de cultures et même de détecter les malades. Donc tout ce qui se trouvait dans les autres applications a été regroupé en une seule application mais accessible par les agriculteurs et qu'ils comprennent directement. Et aujourd'hui quels sont les besoins pour un développement à grand échelle ? Nous avons un besoin immense pour déployer notre infrastructure. Parce que c'est très lourd. Mais la chance peut-être que Sotilma a aujourd'hui, c'est que nous avons déjà avec les objets connectés. Parce que nous avons commencé depuis 2022 par la vente d'équipements pour les agriculteurs, nous avons avec nos objets connectés pu générer 12 millions de flux vidéo par jour, de quoi déjà entraîner une intelligence artificielle. Et d'ici 2030, nous avons l'ambition d'aller vers 400 millions de flux vidéo annualisés en données agricoles et en données d'irrigation. Donc pour cela, il faut forcément un soutien d'investisseurs, de partenaires pour déployer cette intelligence artificielle, renforcer notre infrastructure et surtout avoir des pilotes avec les institutions agricoles, les grands producteurs et les agrobusiness. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Remove Larabanga Mosque from new GH¢2 note, they’re intolerant of other religions – Christian group tells BoG
items.description: A Christian advocacy group, the Alliance of Christian Apologists, Ghana, has asked the Government and the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to take the Larabanga Mosque off the new GH¢2 banknote before the Heritage Series notes go into circulation on December 1, 2026. The group says it accepts the mosque as an important Islamic heritage site. Its objection is to the mosque being presented on the national currency as a symbol of religious tolerance and diversity. It argues that the history of the Larabanga community contradicts that message. “Religious heritage is not the same thing as religious tolerance,” the Alliance said in a press statement dated November 16, 2026. What’s on the GH¢2 note The GH¢2 note is one of eight denominations in the Heritage Series. President John Dramani Mahama unveiled the series at the Bank Square in Accra on Thursday, November 12. Its theme is religious freedom. The orange-and-gold note carries the portrait of Cardinal Peter Poreku Dery (1918–2008) on the front. He was the former Catholic Archbishop of Tamale and became Ghana’s second cardinal in 2006, after Cardinal Peter Turkson. He stands for the Christian faith on the note. The reverse shows the Larabanga Mosque in the West Gonja area of the Savannah Region. It is a mud-and-timber building in the Sudanese style, traditionally dated to 1421, and is widely regarded as one of the oldest mosques in West Africa. It is often called the “Mecca of West Africa.” The mosque also appeared on the reverse of the ¢5 note in the 1970s. The note’s Adinkra symbol is Nyame Dua, meaning “tree of God.” It represents God’s presence, protection and spiritual guidance, and points to Ghana’s indigenous spiritual heritage. The group’s case The Alliance cites public reporting, including a Daily Graphic report, in which Larabanga community leaders said churches and traditional shrines have historically not been allowed to operate in the community. According to the report, the leaders said this followed the practices of their forefathers. “This creates a fundamental contradiction,” the statement said. “How can a community known for restricting the establishment of other faiths’ places of worship be presented on Ghana’s national currency as a symbol of religious tolerance and diversity?” The group said national currency “is more than money. It is a representation of who we are and what we choose to celebrate as a nation.” Putting the mosque on the note under a tolerance narrative, it argued, “risks rewarding religious exclusivity with national recognition and sends the wrong message to future generations.” Under the heading “Ghana Has Better Stories to Tell,” the Alliance asked government to look beyond religious monuments. It wants recognition for the pioneers of Ghana’s education and teacher-training institutions, healthcare and medical institutions, vocational and technical training, and constitutional and democratic institutions, along with the foundations of national development. “Our national story belongs to all Ghanaians, as well as non-Ghanaians who contributed meaningfully to the development of this country,” the statement said. It added: “NOT religious intolerant and extremists’ elements.” MyJoyOnline, as of the time of publication, had not independently verified the group’s claims of religious intolerance. Three demands The Alliance is asking Government and the BoG to: Remove the Larabanga Mosque from the proposed currency before the notes enter circulation in December; Review the criteria used to select monuments and personalities for the national currency; and Give greater consideration to individuals and institutions whose contributions demonstrably advanced education, healthcare, skills development, freedom and democracy in Ghana. The group stressed that its position “is not an attack on Muslims or Islam” and called it “a call for historical honesty and consistency.” “If Larabanga Mosque is presented as an Islamic heritage monument, we have no objection,” it said. “But if it is presented as a symbol of religious tolerance and diversity, then the historical record demands serious reconsideration.” The statement concluded: “Ghana should not place a symbol of religious exclusivity and intolerance on its currency and call it religious tolerance.” Latest in a string of controversies The Larabanga objection is the latest in a series of disputes over the Heritage Series in the two weeks since its launch. The sharpest has been over the removal of the Big Six. On the current notes, all denominations carry the collective portrait of the six leaders. On the new series, only Dr Kwame Nkrumah remains on the GH¢200 note. Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin accused the Government of trying to erase the other five. He said the decision could remove them from the currency but never from history. NPP figure Dr Boakye Danquah has proposed that each of the six should have had a note of his own. The GH¢50 note has its own dispute. It is meant to honour Theodosia Salome Okoh, designer of the national flag. Her nephew, Prof Eddie Obeng, said the face on it was actually that of his mother, the scientist Dr Letitia Obeng, Mrs Okoh’s younger sister. The BoG denied this. It said the portrait was developed from several photographs of Mrs Okoh, but admitted that adjustments made it resemble her sister. The Alliance of Christian Apologists has taken strong positions on religion in public life before. In September, it rejected calls for Christian mission schools to change their religious character to accommodate Muslim students. It also called for equal enforcement of the law in religious matters. The BoG says the Heritage Series will circulate alongside the existing notes, which remain legal tender and will be withdrawn gradually.

items.title: Benue APC crisis: Why Alia/Akume reconciliation ‘ll not work – Agada
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Factional Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Benue State, Mr Austin Agada, has declared that there is currently no genuine reconciliation between the camps of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume, and Governor Hyacinth Alia, insisting that any peace deal must go beyond preparations for the 2027 general elections. Agada, an ally of Senator Akume, made the position known in a social media exchange with another APC stalwart and Akume loyalist, Mr Abua Yaji, where he explained why previous reconciliation efforts within the ruling party in the state had failed. He maintained that reconciliation could only be meaningful if it addressed the broader concerns of the Benue people, stressing that it must not be reduced to an arrangement designed to secure political advantage ahead of the next elections. According to him, “the truth remains that reconciliation cannot be done on the basis of electioneering alone. If there must be reconciliation in the first place, it has to be genuine, and it will not even be with us, it will be with the Benue people.” Agada recalled the massive support the APC enjoyed from the electorate during the 2023 general elections, arguing that any reconciliation process must take into consideration the expectations and interests of the people who voted for the party. “Reconciliation must be seen to be total in all spheres, considering the level the Benue people came out in the last election in 2023 to vote for our party under my leadership. So, when they are ready for reconciliation, we will know. But for now, there is no reconciliation; they are not ready for reconciliation,” he declared. He, however, clarified that his position did not amount to a rejection of dialogue among party leaders, noting that there was nothing wrong with political stakeholders sitting together to resolve their differences. “The Benue people have their resolve already, it does not matter what anybody thinks about it. But the truth about it is that there is nothing wrong for people to sit down and talk. We are not in a theatre of war. Even in a war situation, people sit down and talk,” he said. Explaining further, Agada described the ongoing engagements among the party leaders as brotherly discussions, insisting that any eventual agreement must be transparent and acceptable to the people of the state. “So, what is going on is that they are talking as brothers, and if it reaches the time for a genuine reconciliation, the entire Benue people will know. People will sit down and people will speak out,” he stated. He stressed that the disagreement within the APC should not be viewed as a personal contest involving Akume or any other political leader, but as an issue concerning the entire party structure and the people of Benue state. “So, it is not about Austin Agada or the SGF, George Akume. It is about the Benue people and the entire leadership of our party from the ward level to the state. We have not foreclosed reconciliation, but it cannot be tailored towards an election,” he added. Agada also questioned the fulfilment of campaign promises made to the people during the 2023 elections, particularly commitments concerning the return of displaced communities in Sankera and the MINDA bloc, as well as alleged governance imbalance and persistent insecurity in Benue South. He said, “Aside from the factionalisation of the party, which was purposefully done, what about the promises we made to the Benue people during the electioneering that I swore round the 23 Local Government Areas?” he queried. Recalling the campaign commitments, he asked, “Like I always say, we promised to bring back home the people of Sankera. Have we done that till today? They contributed money for us, including people in the bush. What about the people of MINDA bloc that have lost their ancestral homes, and we promised them that in our first 100 days in office we will take them back home. What have we done about them? What about the people of Benue South, also known as Zone C (Idoma-speaking area), the imbalance in the system of governance, what about the attacjs and killings in Agatu, Otukpo, Apa, Ogbadibo and even Okpokwu Local Government Areas? These are some of the issues.” The post Benue APC crisis: Why Alia/Akume reconciliation ‘ll not work – Agada appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a donné raison au Sénégal ce mardi 24 novembre 2026. Depuis Lausanne, il a annulé la décision du jury d'appel de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF), qui avait retiré la victoire au Sénégal en finale de la CAN 2025.

items.title: 21e Semaine numérique: le Burkina Faso réaffirme son ambition de souveraineté technologique
items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a présidé, ce mardi 24 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle d’ouverture de la 21 ᵉ é dition de la Semaine du num é rique. Plac é e sous le th è me « Souverainet é technologique : accélérer la transformation digitale sécurisée et inclusive », cette édition se tient du 24 au 27 novembre 2026 au pavillon Soleil Levant du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), avec la participation d’acteurs nationaux et de délégations du Mali et du Niger. ‎ Dans son discours d’ouverture, le Chef du Gouvernement a rappelé que la souveraineté numérique constitue désormais une priorité nationale, conformément à la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Pour lui, cette souveraineté ne saurait se limiter à la disponibilité des infrastructures et des équipements. Elle suppose également la maîtrise des données, le développement des compétences nationales et la capacité de concevoir, d’exploiter et de faire évoluer ses propres solutions technologiques. ‎« Nous devons être capables de prévenir les risques, de rétablir nos services et de décider par nous-mêmes », a-t-il souligné, insistant sur les enjeux liés à la sécurité des infrastructures numériques et à la protection des données. ‎Pour traduire cette ambition en résultats concrets, le Premier ministre a décliné trois grandes priorités de l’action gouvernementale : maîtriser les infrastructures et les données ; simplifier les services publics et développer l’économie numérique ; garantir la sécurité et l’accessibilité des services. Évoquant les deux centres de données modulaires achevés en 2025 pour l’administration, il a insisté sur leur sécurité, leur maintenance et le transfert de compétences aux équipes nationales. Il a également appelé à supprimer les formalités inutiles et à réduire les délais et les déplacements des usagers, tout en intégrant la cybersécurité et la protection des données dès la conception des projets. ‎À l’échelle de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), le Chef du Gouvernement a plaidé pour la mutualisation des infrastructures, le partage des compétences et une réponse coordonnée aux cybermenaces. Intervenant au nom de ses homologues, le ministre malien de la Communication, de l’Économie numérique et de la Modernisation de l’administration, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, a proposé des infrastructures de confiance communes, un bouclier cyber partagé, des cadres juridiques harmonisés et un investissement accru dans les talents. « La souveraineté technologique n’est pas synonyme de repli sur soi. C’est la capacité de choisir nos partenaires, de négocier d’égal à égal et de faire confiance à notre jeunesse », a-t-il affirmé. ‎La 21ᵉ édition de la Semaine du numérique a pour coparrains le Camarade ministre d’État, ministre de l’Administration territoriale, et la Camarade ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité. Prenant la parole en leur nom, la Camarade Passowendé Pélagie Kabré/Kaboré a relevé l’importance du numérique dans la modernisation de l’État et l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Elle a notamment évoqué les possibilités offertes par les outils numériques pour identifier les ménages vulnérables, cibler les interventions sociales et améliorer l’accès aux services publics. Elle a toutefois rappelé que cette transformation doit s’accompagner de garanties solides en matière de sécurité et de confidentialité des données. ‎Devant la presse, la ministre de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Dr Aminata Zerbo-Sabané, a souligné que cette 21ᵉ édition constitue une occasion pour les acteurs de l’écosystème numérique de formuler des propositions et des recommandations en faveur d’une transformation digitale au service du développement national. Elle a particulièrement insisté sur les exigences de sécurité et d’inclusion, deux dimensions indispensables pour éviter que le numérique ne devienne un facteur supplémentaire d’inégalités entre les populations urbaines et rurales. ‎« Au regard de la qualité et de la diversité de ce que les acteurs du numérique ont à exposer, j’invite les élèves, les étudiants et les familles à découvrir les activités au SIAO jusqu’au vendredi 27 novembre », a déclaré le Camarade Premier ministre. Le public est ainsi invité à se rendre au pavillon Soleil Levant du SIAO pour découvrir l’exposition des acteurs du numérique. ‎Au-delà des communications officielles, la 21ᵉ Semaine du numérique se veut également une vitrine du savoir-faire et de la créativité des acteurs nationaux. Plusieurs activités sont inscrites au programme, notamment le village des start-up, le Data Challenge, le hacking éthique et les compétitions de robotique. Le 13ᵉ Forum sur la gouvernance de l’Internet et le 5ᵉ Forum sur les noms de domaine permettront également d’approfondir les réflexions sur la gouvernance numérique et les perspectives liées à l’intelligence artificielle. DCRP/Primature L’article 21e Semaine numérique: le Burkina Faso réaffirme son ambition de souveraineté technologique est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Tinubu needs no presidential debate, policies are clear — Showunmi
items.description: …PDP chieftain urges Ogun residents to mobilise votes, cautions against political violence By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Convener of the Alternative Movement and chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Otunba Segun Showunmi, has dismissed calls for President Bola Tinubu to participate in a presidential debate ahead of the 2027 general elections, arguing that the President has sufficiently communicated his policies, programmes and vision to Nigerians. Showunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, maintained that a presidential debate was unnecessary, insisting that Tinubu’s policy direction and philosophy of governance were already clear to the electorate. He argued that the primary purpose of a presidential debate was to enable voters to understand candidates’ policies, programmes and development agendas, a responsibility he said Tinubu had already fulfilled through his engagements with Nigerians. “When it comes to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, his policy direction is very clear. We are now on the journey to prosperity. His guiding principles of governance are equally clear: an inclusive, united and indivisible Nigeria that works for everyone,” he said. Describing Tinubu’s leadership style as accessible, relatable, pragmatic and intelligent, Showunmi said the President was under no obligation to participate in a debate merely to satisfy public expectations. “Even if we were to bring the candidates together for a debate, who exactly would he be debating? Is it Peter Obi, who, when asked a question, will run to Malaysia, or the other man, whose name I would rather not mention?” he asked. He added: “The debate has already conducted itself.” Showunmi, however, acknowledged that the final decision on whether to participate in a presidential debate rested with Tinubu, saying the President could either engage his opponents or rely on his previous interactions with the electorate. “If the President decides to participate in a debate, that is entirely up to him. If he decides that he has already engaged with the people at a level where they understand his message, that is also his prerogative,” he said. He likened calls for Tinubu to debate opposition candidates to asking a headmaster to participate in a speaking contest with primary school pupils. Turning to the party’s electoral preparations in Ogun State, Showunmi urged residents to prioritise grassroots mobilisation and voter participation rather than become distracted by political arguments. He said the immediate challenge facing the campaign team was to ensure that Tinubu secured a substantial share of the votes in Ogun State. “His victory is no longer in question; we are winning. What we are working towards now is ensuring that our numbers are also respectable,” he declared. Showunmi questioned why Ogun State, with an estimated 3.5 million votes, should fail to record an impressive electoral performance compared with other states. “When you look at the numbers from other states, some people will record one million votes, while others will record two million. Why should we behave like illiterates in Ogun State when we have 3.5 million votes?” he queried. He called on residents to intensify mobilisation, encourage eligible voters to participate and ensure peaceful conduct on election day. Showunmi also expressed optimism that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) would conduct a credible election capable of strengthening Nigeria’s democratic image before the international community. “The earlier we come out and motivate ourselves to participate on that one day, the better. That is all I am asking of them. By the grace of God Almighty, we will secure the maximum number of available votes in Ogun State,” he said. On the political dynamics in Ogun State, Showunmi reaffirmed his commitment to following the political direction of Governor Dapo Abiodun while maintaining his support for Tinubu’s presidential ambition. He said his loyalty to the President was unquestionable, citing his membership of two presidential campaign councils. “What we know is that I have told my people that wherever Governor Dapo Abiodun goes, I will follow. I have also specifically told them that, when it comes to the presidential campaign, they do not even need to ask where I stand, considering that I am a member of two critical campaign councils of the President,” he said. Showunmi explained that his immediate responsibility was to mobilise support for Tinubu while awaiting further political instructions from the Ogun State governor. “Therefore, I have come here to mobilise them on behalf of the President while waiting for Governor Dapo Abiodun to tell me who else he wants me to support,” he stated. Speaking on the Rainbow Coalition, a political platform reportedly comprising individuals from different political parties supporting Tinubu, Showunmi said the initiative had created an opportunity for broader political cooperation. He noted, however, that the coalition’s political identity in Ogun State appeared closely associated with Governor Abiodun. “As far as we are concerned, those who have created what they call the Rainbow Coalition have provided a platform for people from other political parties to come together and support the President,” he said. “However, as far as Ogun State is concerned, I have a feeling that the Rainbow is the Rainbow of Dapo Abiodun.” Showunmi also called for an end to political violence and the use of young people to perpetrate criminal activities, urging parents, families and community leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their members. He argued that those who instigated ordinary citizens to engage in violence should be held accountable, noting that perpetrators were often members of the same communities rather than outsiders. “Angels do not kill people, and neither do the children of the Pope come here carrying sticks. More often than not, they are our own children and our own people, instigated by characters I describe as scallywags,” he said. He added that anyone who instigated ordinary people to engage in criminal activities deserved to be condemned. Showunmi urged politicians and their supporters not to allow electoral contests and political disagreements to destroy relationships or destabilise communities, reminding them that elections were temporary and political opponents would continue to coexist after the polls. “At the end of the day, elections come once every four years. After we have conducted this election and Bola Ahmed Tinubu has won overwhelmingly, another election will still come,” he added. He also cautioned APC supporters against complacency, saying his political engagements outside Ogun State had convinced him that Tinubu enjoyed substantial support in other parts of the country. “I am even afraid that the President may secure more votes in the North than here, despite the reason I have been appealing to my people,” he said. “I have been around, and the support for him out there is massive. I do not want a situation where the support at home, or the numbers we record here, become disappointingly low because of our attitude.” He renewed his appeal to eligible voters across Ogun State to intensify grassroots mobilisation, shun violence and participate actively in the electoral process. The post Tinubu needs no presidential debate, policies are clear — Showunmi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Quand les paysans prennent la parole : le plaidoyer paysan, un levain pour l'agroécologie au Burkina Faso
items.description: Introduction Ce document de vulgarisation est tiré de l'article scientifique de fond intitulé : « Savoirs endogènes et politiques publiques : le plaidoyer paysan comme levain de l'innovation agroécologique au Burkina Faso », TOUGRl Kayabila, Patrice KOURAOGO, in « Espaces, sociétés et développement durable en Afrique subsaharienne », publié dans les Editions du CNRST, Janvier 2026, pages 482- 496, ISBN : 978-2-494747-12-8. Au Burkina Faso, beaucoup de producteurs connaissent l'agroécologie sans toujours employer ce mot. Le zaï, les cordons pierreux, le fumier de parc, le compost, l'association du mil et du niébé dans le même poquet sont des pratiques qui nourrissent la terre au lieu de l'épuiser. Elles sont au cœur de ce que les spécialistes appellent l'agroécologie, c'est-à-dire une manière de produire qui s'appuie sur la nature, sur les ressources locales et sur les savoirs des paysans plutôt que sur les engrais et les pesticides chimiques achetés. Depuis 2023, le pays dispose d'une Stratégie nationale de développement de l'agroécologie (SND-AE 2023-2027), adoptée par le ministère en charge de l'agriculture (Burkina Faso, 2023). C'est une avancée importante. Pourtant, sur le terrain, les acteurs constatent que ces pratiques restent moins répandues que ne le souhaitent les spécialistes et les pouvoirs publics. Pourquoi ? Et comment les paysans eux-mêmes peuvent-ils faire bouger les choses ? Cet article répond à ces questions en s'adressant d'abord aux producteurs et productrices et à leurs organisations, mais aussi aux agents d'appui-conseil, aux élus locaux, aux décideurs, aux journalistes, aux étudiants et aux consommateurs. Il s'inspire de l'article source et s'enrichi des données d'une thèse de doctorat consacrée à une organisation paysanne dénommée, Association Minim Sông Pânga du Burkina Faso (AMSP-Burkina) ainsi que des travaux d'un atelier régional de l'Alliance pour l'Agroécologie en Afrique de l'Ouest (3AO), tenu à Ouagadougou en mai 2026. Mots pour comprendre • Savoirs endogènes : connaissances et savoir-faire que les producteurs reconnaissent comme les leurs, parce qu'ils viennent de leur expérience ou qu'ils les ont adoptés et adaptés au fil du temps. • Agroécologie : manière de produire qui s'appuie sur les processus naturels (vie du sol, diversité des cultures, arbres, recyclage) et sur les ressources locales. • Plaidoyer : ensemble d'actions organisées pour faire changer une décision, une règle ou une pratique au profit d'une cause. • Bio-intrants : produits naturels fabriqués localement pour nourrir le sol (compost, biofertilisants) ou protéger les cultures (extraits de neem, de piment…). Méthodologie Menée entre 2022 et 2025 dans quatre communes du Burkina Faso, cette recherche s'appuie sur une immersion auprès de l'Association Minim Sông Pânga du Burkina Faso (AMSP-Burkina), combinant questionnaires auprès de 203 producteurs et productrices, 54 entretiens, 6 discussions de groupe et des observations de terrain. Elle a également intégré une étude complémentaire auprès de 30 personnes ressources sur la prise en compte des savoirs paysans dans les politiques agricoles, ainsi que l'analyse de documents publics. Enfin, la participation du premier auteur à un atelier régional de la 3AO, réunissant 84 acteurs de plusieurs pays ouest-africains, a permis de mettre en perspective l'expérience burkinabè à l'échelle sous régionale. Résultats 1. Les paysans ne partent pas de zéro Les chiffres de l'enquête sont parlants. Parmi les 203 producteurs interrogés, près de 8 sur 10 pratiquent les cordons pierreux, 2 sur 3 utilisent le fumier de parc ou le compost, plus de la moitié font du zaï, associent les cultures dans le même poquet ou alternent céréales et légumineuses d'une saison à l'autre. Les producteurs observent le ruissellement de l'eau pendant les pluies pour placer leurs aménagements, laissent des touffes d'herbe pour retenir la terre et lisent dans le comportement des insectes et des oiseaux l'arrivée de la saison. D'autres travaux avaient déjà montré l'inventivité des paysans burkinabè, en particulier autour du zaï amélioré (Kaboré et Reij, 2004 ; Dialla, 2005). Un fait a particulièrement retenu l'attention. Beaucoup de ces pratiques, présentées aujourd'hui comme « celles des anciens », ont en réalité été améliorées ou introduites assez récemment, avec l'appui de projets ou des services techniques. Dans la zone d'étude, près de 9 producteurs sur 10 reconnaissent que leurs parents ne pratiquaient pas le zaï comme ils le font aujourd'hui. Pourtant, ces techniques sont désormais revendiquées comme un héritage. Un producteur de Nagréongo résume ce sentiment. Pour lui, rien de ce que l'on appelle aujourd'hui « agroécologie » n'est nouveau ; c'est ce que faisaient déjà les pères et les grands-pères. Ce constat est important et montre que les savoirs paysans ne sont pas figés. Ils se transforment, intègrent des apports extérieurs, puis les font leurs. La recherche appelle ce processus l'« endogénéisation ». Une innovation est mieux acceptée quand les producteurs y reconnaissent le prolongement de ce qu'ils savent déjà faire. L'expression en mooré, employée pour désigner l'agroécologie (Koglezang-koobo) est beaucoup significatif. 2. Une organisation paysanne qui sert de pont L'Association Minim Sông Pânga du Burkina Faso (AMSP-Burkina), fait le lien entre les champs, la recherche et les autorités. Dans les villages, elle anime des groupes de producteurs qui testent eux-mêmes, dans leurs propres champs, différentes techniques proposées par les chercheurs : variétés, compost de type Bokashi, semis en lignes, biopesticides à base de neem. Les producteurs comparent les résultats, discutent entre eux et choisissent ce qui convient à leurs sols, à leur main-d'œuvre et à leurs moyens. L'association a aussi une idée originale. Elle cale ses activités sur les fêtes coutumières et sur le calendrier social des villages, et associe les chefs coutumiers. Les journées agroécologiques organisées à Korsimoro en 2024 ont ainsi rassemblé producteurs, chercheurs et autorités autour de démonstrations et de débats en mooré et en français. Lors de ces débats, ce sont les francophones qui ont dû, pour une fois, attendre la traduction. Cette démarche est appréciée par 6 producteurs sur 10 qui estiment que l'association valorise bien leurs savoirs. Mais 4 sur 10 émettent des réserves. Certains regrettent que les semences proposées viennent surtout de la recherche et sont inaccessibles, d'autres participent peu aux activités ou attendent encore des appuis matériels. Les observations montrent aussi que, dans les réunions, la parole reste souvent dominée par les hommes âgés, malgré les efforts pour faire parler les femmes et les jeunes. 3. Le plaidoyer commence au village On imagine souvent le plaidoyer comme une affaire de bureaux et de ministères. L'étude montre qu'il commence en réalité au village, entre paysans. C'est ce que nous appelons le plaidoyer horizontal. Dans les comités agroécologiques villageois, dans les assemblées et les ateliers communaux, les producteurs montrent leurs résultats, convainquent leurs voisins et cherchent à changer des règles qui freinent les bonnes pratiques. Un exemple concret à travers la règle du prêt de terre. Celui qui cultive une parcelle empruntée hésite à y faire du zaï ou des cordons pierreux. Il s'interdit d'y planter des arbres ou de pratiquer la régénération naturelle assistée (RNA). La justification est simple : si la terre devient fertile, le propriétaire risque de la reprendre. Tant que cette règle ne change pas, aucun conseil technique ne suffira. En portant cette question devant les assemblées villageoises et les chefs coutumiers, les paysans touchent au cœur du problème. Ce plaidoyer horizontal prépare le plaidoyer vertical, celui qui s'adresse aux autorités. L'AMSP-Burkina participe à des coalitions régionales et nationales et à des espaces d'échanges internationaux avec des chercheurs et des partenaires. Les personnes interrogées sont nettes. En effet, plus de 7 sur 10 pensent que les paysans et leurs organisations sont les mieux placés pour porter ce plaidoyer. Elles ajoutent qu'ils gagnent à s'allier aux chercheurs, aux ONG et aux cadres de l'administration. Comme l'a dit un producteur d'Andemtenga, nul n'est mieux placé que celui qui a mal pour dire son mal. 4. Des politiques qui progressent, mais pas assez vite L'analyse des grands documents de politique agricole, du Programme d'ajustement structurel des années 1990 jusqu'à la SND-AE, montre une évolution réelle. Pendant longtemps, les savoirs paysans n'y apparaissaient pas. Ils sont aujourd'hui explicitement mentionnés. Mais sur le terrain, la perception reste critique : plus de 75 % des personnes ressources estiment que ces savoirs sont encore peu pris en compte, et 10 % qu'ils sont ignorés. Seules 15 % sont satisfaites. La raison principale tient à une tension entre deux logiques. La première cherche à produire plus, vite, grâce aux engrais chimiques et aux machines. Elle mobilise chaque année des milliards de francs CFA de subventions. La seconde cherche à produire durablement, en prenant soin du sol et en valorisant les ressources locales. Une personne ressource l'a dit sans détour. Estimant que la priorité d'un ministre de l'Agriculture est « d'abord que la population ait à manger », d'où la tentation de miser sur les intrants chimiques. Des signaux encourageants existent néanmoins. Lors de l'atelier de la 3AO, le ministère burkinabè en charge de l'agriculture a indiqué subventionner environ 3 600 tonnes de fumure organique par an. Mieux, cela fait déjà quelques années que le ministère a désigné un point focal pour l'agroécologie. Sans vouloir en attribuer tout le mérite aux organisations paysanes, le plaidoyer paysan a sans doute contribué à ces avancées, aux côtés d'autres acteurs. 5. Trois combats communs à l'Afrique de l'Ouest L'atelier régional de la 3AO a montré que les préoccupations burkinabè sont partagées dans toute la sous-région. Trois priorités ont été retenues pour le plaidoyer des années 2026-2030. La première concerne les semences paysannes. Selon la note de plaidoyer de la 3AO, ces semences, sélectionnées, conservées et échangées par les paysans, en particulier par les femmes, fournissent la grande majorité des semences utilisées par les exploitations familiales. Elles sont pourtant peu reconnues par les lois. La deuxième porte sur les biofertilisants et biostimulants : face à des engrais importés dont les prix ont fortement augmenté depuis 2021, produire localement des fertilisants naturels permet de réduire la dépendance et de régénérer les sols. La troisième concerne les bio-protecteurs : des extraits de neem, de piment ou d'autres plantes locales peuvent remplacer une partie des pesticides chimiques, dont l'usage a fortement augmenté dans la région et qui menacent la santé des producteurs et des consommateurs. Les participants ont aussi tenu un discours de vérité. Les bio-intrants ne sont ni gratuits ni toujours faciles à fabriquer. Leur efficacité doit être mieux démontrée, et il vaut mieux parler de « toxicité moindre » que de produits « sans danger ». Le plaidoyer gagne en crédibilité lorsqu'il s'appuie sur des preuves solides et sur l'expérience des producteurs. Ce qu'il faut retenir • Les paysans burkinabè disposent de savoirs riches et vivants, qui intègrent aussi des innovations venues d'ailleurs. • Une innovation est mieux adoptée quand elle prolonge ce que les producteurs savent déjà faire. • Les organisations paysannes servent de pont entre les champs, la recherche et les autorités. • Le plaidoyer commence au village, entre paysans, avant de toucher les décideurs. • Les politiques progressent, mais les subventions favorisent encore surtout les intrants chimiques. Conclusion L'agroécologie n'est pas seulement une affaire de techniques. C'est aussi une affaire de reconnaissance et de parole. Les résultats présentés ici montrent que les producteurs burkinabè ne sont pas de simples bénéficiaires de projets : ils expérimentent, adaptent, transmettent, et ils savent se faire entendre lorsqu'ils s'organisent. Pour que ce levain fasse lever toute la pâte, chacun a un rôle à jouer. Les producteurs et leurs organisations peuvent documenter leurs résultats, partager leurs expériences de paysan à paysan et veiller à ce que les femmes et les jeunes aient toute leur place dans les décisions. Les chercheurs peuvent associer davantage les producteurs à l'interprétation des essais, et pas seulement à leur mise en place. Les élus locaux peuvent inscrire l'agroécologie dans les plans communaux de développement et soutenir les discussions sur le prêt de terre. Les décideurs nationaux peuvent donner à la SND-AE des moyens à la hauteur de ses ambitions, rééquilibrer les subventions en faveur de la fumure organique et des bio-intrants, et reconnaître les semences paysannes. Enfin, les médias, en particulier les radios communautaires, et les consommateurs peuvent faire connaître et acheter les produits issus de l'agroécologie. Comme le rappelle un proverbe cité par une participante au cours des travaux de la 3AO, « la graine ne refuse pas de pousser », encore faut-il lui offrir un bon terreau. Ce terreau, ce sont des politiques qui écoutent ceux qui cultivent la terre. Références bibliographiques 3AO, 2026b, Notes politiques : Systèmes semenciers paysans ; Biofertilisants et biostimulants ; Bio-protecteurs en Afrique de l'Ouest, à l'intention des dirigeants ouest-africains. BURKINA FASO, Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, 2023, Stratégie nationale de développement de l'agroécologie (SND-AE) 2023-2027, Ouagadougou. DIALLA Basga Émile, 2005, Pratiques et savoirs paysans au Burkina Faso : une présentation de quelques études de cas, Ouagadougou, CAPES. KABORÉ Daniel et REIJ Chris, 2004, The Emergence and Spreading of an Improved Traditional Soil and Water Conservation Practice in Burkina Faso, EPTD Discussion Paper n° 114, Washington, IFPRI. TOUGRI Kayabila, 2025, Savoirs endogènes et plaidoyer paysan pour l'appropriation des innovations agroécologiques en milieu rural : cas de l'Association Minim Sông Pânga du Burkina Faso, thèse de doctorat unique, Ouagadougou, Université Joseph KI-ZERBO, 248 pages. TOUGRI Kayabila et KOURAOGO Patrice, 2026, « Savoirs endogènes et politiques publiques : le plaidoyer paysan comme levain de l'innovation agroécologique au Burkina Faso », in Espaces, sociétés et développement durable en Afrique subsaharienne, Ouagadougou, Éditions du CNRST, pp. 482-496.

items.title: 2027: SDP urges police, security agencies to be impartial
items.description: Party calls for accountability, says culture of impunity must be confronted By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional, impartial, firm and fair in handling electoral activities, warning against the use of security institutions to advance partisan interests. The party also called for an end to the culture of impunity, insisting that perpetrators of political violence must be held accountable irrespective of their political affiliations or status. National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, made the call on Tuesday at a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, in Abuja. Gombe said every political party must be assured that its candidates, supporters, offices and campaign rallies would receive equal protection under the law. “Not some parties. Not the powerful. Every party. Every electorate,” he said. He warned that security must never be perceived as a tool for political advantage, stressing that public confidence would be eroded if citizens believed security agencies were aligned with particular political interests. According to him, threats reported to security agencies must attract prompt responses, incidents of violence must be thoroughly investigated, while identified offenders must face the law irrespective of their political affiliations. The SDP chairman said the culture of impunity must also be confronted, warning that failure to punish perpetrators of political violence could encourage others to engage in similar acts. “When perpetrators of political violence go unpunished, we send a dangerous message to the next person: that violence is acceptable, that it is cheap, and that it pays. Accountability is not vengeance. It is the foundation of deterrence,” he said. Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to peaceful political participation, respect for the rule of law and the protection of the democratic rights of every Nigerian. He urged SDP members, candidates, supporters and campaign organisations to conduct themselves responsibly, saying the party would compete through ideas, persuasion, peaceful mobilisation and constructive dialogue. “Let me be clear: peace must be built on fairness and justice. “Every Nigerian must be free to support the party of their choice without intimidation. Every candidate must be able to campaign without fear. Every party must be able to organise within the law. And every citizen, the farmer in the village, the trader in the market, the young graduate searching for opportunity, must have confidence that their vote and their voice truly matter,” he said. The SDP chairman condemned political thuggery, hate speech, mobilisation of armed groups, destruction of campaign materials, attacks on rallies and party offices, and attempts to disrupt lawful political activities. He said political violence was often a consequence of the actions and decisions of political leaders, particularly their statements at rallies and their failure to caution supporters against misconduct. “Political opponents are not enemies. They are fellow citizens. We may disagree on policy, on ideology, and on leadership, but we share one country and one destiny. We are Nigerians first, before we are politicians,” he said. Gombe challenged political party leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their members and supporters, insisting that condemnation of violence must extend to offenders within their own political organisations. He said the SDP was committed to disciplining any member found engaging in or inciting violence and urged other political parties to adopt similar measures. “Peace cannot merely be preached. It must be practised,” he added. Addressing the police and other security agencies, Gombe said their conduct in the months leading to the elections would significantly influence public confidence in the electoral process. He also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and political parties to ensure compliance with the Electoral Act and other regulations governing political activities. The SDP chairman said many confrontations during political campaigns could be avoided through timely communication, coordination and clarity over rally venues, schedules, routes and required permissions. He called for improved cooperation among security agencies, INEC and political parties to ensure that disagreements over campaign arrangements were resolved before escalating into violence. Gombe said the 2027 general elections would test not only the political preparedness of stakeholders but also their collective commitment to democracy. He urged political actors to pursue their ambitions without endangering the lives, property and dignity of fellow Nigerians. “Our duty is greater than our personal ambitions. It is greater than the interests of any party. It is a duty to this nation and to the generations who will inherit whatever we leave behind,” he said. He expressed the SDP’s readiness to work with the police, INEC, other political parties and stakeholders to ensure that the 2027 electoral process was peaceful, credible, inclusive and reflective of the will of Nigerians. The meeting was convened by the Inspector-General of Police amid concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, including attacks on campaign rallies, destruction of billboards and other campaign materials, and threats to public peace. items.title: Tinubu nominates Dabiri as NASC commissioner
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has forwarded the nomination of Agboola Lukman Dabiri to the Senate for screening and confirmation as Commissioner representing the South-West at the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC). Tinubu’s request was conveyed in a letter read on the floor of the Senate on Monday by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. In the letter, the President said the nomination was made pursuant to subsection 4 of the National Assembly Service Commission Act 2014. “I am pleased to forward for confirmation by the Senate the appointment of Agboola Lukman Dabiri as Commissioner representing South-West at the National Assembly Service Commission. “While I hope that the Senate will consider and confirm the nominee in its usual expeditious manner, please accept, Distinguished Senate and Distinguished Senate President, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu said. The President urged the Senate to consider and confirm Dabiri’s nomination. Akpabio disclosed that the nominee’s curriculum vitae was attached to the letter for the lawmakers’ reference. He subsequently referred the request to the Senate Committee on Establishment, which is expected to report back to the chamber within two weeks. The Senate President said the timeframe was considered appropriate given the current campaign period. Dabiri is expected to replace Taiwo Oluga, who resigned from the commission to contest in the 2027 general elections. items.title: Oyo 2027: ‘I won’t step down for anyone,’ ADC guber candidate vows
items.description: By Adeola Badru The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adegboyega Adegoke, has dismissed rumours that he is planning to withdraw from the 2027 governorship race, declaring that he is determined to contest and win the election. Adegoke, who described himself as a committed contender in the race, said he would not step down for any candidate under any circumstances, insisting that his ambition was driven by his determination to implement his policy agenda, tagged SOLUTIONS, for the benefit of residents of the state. The ADC candidate made his position known in a statement issued by his media team on Tuesday, in which he described the reports of his planned withdrawal as unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. He said he remained resolute in his ambition to become the next governor of Oyo State, adding that he was not in the race as a placeholder for any other candidate. “Let me state unequivocally that I am not stepping down for anybody. I am in this race to win and become the next occupier of the Agodi Governor’s Office,” Adegoke said. He added: “The rumour is unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. I have stated many times that I am not a placeholder. I am the Oyo State governorship candidate of our great party, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the next Executive Governor of Oyo State, Insha Allah.” Adegoke said his ambition was anchored on his determination to deliver the promises contained in his SOLUTIONS agenda, which he said was designed to address the needs of the people and improve their welfare. He urged his supporters across the state to remain steadfast and not allow the rumours to distract them from the campaign, assuring them that he remained fully committed to the governorship contest. The ADC candidate attributed the speculation to individuals who, according to him, were unsettled by his growing popularity and prospects of victory at the polls. He further expressed confidence that his ambition would be realised, declaring that no individual or group could frustrate what he described as God’s plan for his emergence as the next governor of Oyo State. “Nobody can stop the plan of God to make me the next Executive Governor of Oyo State,” he said. items.title: Northern governors dissolve NNDC board, order reorganisation
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The 19 Northern States, which jointly own the New Nigerian Development Company (NNDC), have resolved to dissolve its Board of Directors and constitute a new one as part of efforts to reposition the company. The decision was taken by the Secretaries to the Governments of the 19 Northern States, representing their respective state governments as shareholders, at a Special General Meeting held in Kaduna on Tuesday. However, the dissolution will take effect upon the valid adoption of the relevant ordinary resolutions at a duly convened General Meeting and compliance with applicable statutory requirements. Addressing journalists after the meeting, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, said the shareholders had resolved to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation and repositioning of the company. He said the exercise was aimed at strengthening NNDC’s institutional capacity, improving corporate governance, enhancing operational efficiency and repositioning it as a viable investment and development institution serving the collective economic interests of the 19 Northern States. Njodi disclosed that a new Board of Directors would be constituted to provide strategic leadership, effective supervision, policy direction and corporate oversight. He said the composition, nomination and appointment of the new board would reflect the ownership interests of the participating states, the provisions of the company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the requirements of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020. According to him, shareholders would subsequently approve the nominations and appointments of the new directors in accordance with the company’s constitutional documents and applicable laws. The Gombe SSG said the incoming board, upon its lawful constitution, had been directed to undertake a comprehensive review of the company’s existing management structure, personnel, administrative arrangements, operational framework and performance. He added that the new board would take appropriate measures to reorganise and strengthen the company’s management to promote accountability, professionalism and improved corporate performance, in line with its statutory and fiduciary responsibilities and applicable employment laws. Njodi further disclosed that the incoming board would conduct a comprehensive corporate governance, financial, administrative and operational audit of the company. He said the audit would examine NNDC’s financial position, assets and liabilities, existing investments, subsidiaries, joint ventures and commercial interests. It would also assess the performance and profitability of the company’s investments, compliance with statutory, regulatory and corporate governance obligations, as well as existing contractual commitments and outstanding obligations. The effectiveness of the previous board and management structure, alongside other matters considered necessary for protecting and advancing shareholders’ interests, would also come under review. According to Njodi, the findings and recommendations of the audit would be presented to shareholders at a subsequent General Meeting. He said the outgoing board and management would be required, upon the lawful assumption of office by their successors, to facilitate an orderly handover of the company’s affairs, including records, books of account, statutory documents, financial records, assets, properties, contracts and other relevant institutional materials. Njodi added that the incoming board would ensure that all company assets and interests were adequately protected during the transition, warning against any unauthorised disposal, transfer, encumbrance or alienation of the company’s assets. He explained that shareholders had earlier reviewed the company’s current state of affairs, including its corporate governance structure, operational performance, management arrangements and the effectiveness of the existing board. The shareholders, he said, considered a comprehensive reorganisation necessary in the overriding interests of the company, its owners and the economic development aspirations of Northern Nigeria. Njodi said the shareholders were exercising their statutory powers under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, particularly Section 288, which provides for the removal of directors by ordinary resolution, subject to compliance with the applicable statutory procedures and the company’s Articles of Association. He said the decision was also driven by the desire to restore confidence, accountability, transparency, professionalism and effective corporate governance in the administration of the company.
